https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-broc.instructions:
Gather and prep
Gather ingredients. Roughly chop the broccoli florets.
Slice the chicken
Cut the chicken breast tenderloins into bite-size pieces. (You can totally use chicken thighs or whole breasts for this recipe. I just saw these tenderloins at the grocery store and the price was right!).
Season the chicken
Transfer the chicken to a medium mixing bowl with 1 tsp salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika. Toss until evenly coated.
Brown the chicken
Melt butter and olive oil in a large broiler pan or an oven-safe sauté pan over medium heat. Add seasoned chicken.
Cook chicken through
Cook until the chicken is cooked through, about 6 minutes per side, 12-15 minutes total.
Toast the orzo
Next, add the orzo to the pan and toss it with the chicken to lightly toast it, about 2 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with the chicken broth. Stir everything together and turn the heat down to medium-low.
Turn broiler on
Shred cheddar cheese and set aside. Set oven to broil on high.
Add the milk
Add room temperature whole milk to the skillet and stir to combine.
Simmer until cooked
Add chopped broccoli florets. Simmer everything for about 8 minutes or until the orzo is done to your liking, and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
Make it cheesy
Stir in half of the cheddar cheese.
Add toppings
Add the rest of the cheddar cheese on top and sprinkle with the remaining salt and any extra pepper you might like.
Broil the casserole
Transfer to oven and broil for 3-5 minutes until the cheese has melted, or just put the lid on your pan and melt the cheese on the stovetop.

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/harves.description: These easy Harvest Chicken Bowls combine juicy seasoned chicken thighs, roasted sweet potatoes, crisp apples, kale, cranberries and pecans with a sweet and tangy maple Dijon dressing. They're packed with fall flavor, high in protein and ready in about 30 minutes!

ingredients: 1 large sweet potato (peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes, about 3 cups)
1 1/2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 5–6 thighs)
1 small garlic clove (finely grated or minced)
1 crisp red apple (such as Honeycrisp or Pink Lady, thinly sliced)
1 large sweet potato (peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes, about 3 cups)
1 1/2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 5–6 thighs)
1 small garlic clove (finely grated or minced)
1 crisp red apple (such as Honeycrisp or Pink Lady, thinly sliced)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/harves.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Add the sweet potatoes to the pan and toss with the avocado oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Spread into a single layer and roast for 18–20 minutes, tossing once about halfway through, until browned around the edges and tender, keeping the cubes close to 1/2 inch is important so they cook quickly.
While the sweet potatoes begin roasting, pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season both sides with the garlic powder, smoked paprika, thyme, onion powder, salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the avocado oil. Add the chicken thighs in a single layer and cook, undisturbed, for about 5–6 minutes on the first side, until deeply golden brown. Flip and cook for another 4–6 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and reaches at least 165°F internally. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and allow it to rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
While the chicken and sweet potatoes cook, whisk together the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, garlic, salt and pepper until well combined and emulsified. Taste and adjust the salt or maple syrup as desired.
Place the chopped kale in a large bowl and drizzle with about 1 tablespoon of the maple Dijon dressing. Massage with clean hands for about 30–60 seconds, until the kale becomes slightly darker and softer but still has plenty of structure.
After resting, slice each chicken thigh across the grain into approximately 1/2-inch slices.
Divide the massaged kale among four bowls. Top with roasted sweet potatoes, sliced chicken, apple slices, dried cranberries and pecans. Drizzle generously with the remaining maple Dijon dressing and serve.

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/pan-seared.description: This easy pan-seared chicken breasts recipe makes juicy, tender chicken with a beautifully golden crust right on the stovetop.

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, about 6 to 8 ounces each
1 teaspoon fine sea salt (only needed if you are not brining)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons avocado oil or other neutral high-heat oil
4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, about 6 to 8 ounces each
1 teaspoon fine sea salt (only needed if you are not brining)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons avocado oil or other neutral high-heat oil
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/pan-seared.instructions:
Pound the chicken. Place the chicken breasts between two sheets of parchment paper or plastic wrap. Gently pound the thicker portions until each breast is an even ½- to ¾-inch thickness.
Brine the chicken, optional. Check the package to make sure the chicken has not already been brined or enhanced with a sodium solution. Stir the fine sea salt into 2 cups lukewarm water until dissolved, then stir in the remaining 2 cups cold water. Add the chicken and let it brine for 15 to 30 minutes. Remove the chicken from the brine and pat it very dry with paper towels.
Season the chicken. Season the chicken evenly on both sides with the black pepper. If you skipped the brine, also season it with the 1 teaspoon fine sea salt. If you brined the chicken, do not add any more salt.
Sear the first side. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the oil is shimmering, add the chicken breasts in a single layer. Cook without moving them for 3 to 5 minutes, until deeply golden underneath and opaque about halfway up the sides.
Flip and finish cooking. Flip the chicken breasts and reduce the heat to medium. Continue cooking uncovered for 3 to 5 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and registers 155-160°F in the thickest portion. (The chicken will continue cooking after being removed from the heat to reach the safe 165°F temperature for eating.) Reduce the heat to medium-low if the chicken begins browning too quickly.
Rest the chicken. Transfer the chicken to a clean plate and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
Deglaze the pan, optional. While the pan is still very hot, carefully pour ¼ cup water or chicken broth into the skillet. Use a wooden spoon to scrape up the flavorful browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until slightly reduced, then pour the pan drippings over the chicken.
Serve. Slice the chicken against the grain and serve warm.

https://www.loveandlemons.com/pasta-alla.description: Pasta alla Norma is a classic Italian pasta dish that comes from Sicily. It's tossed in a rich, flavorful tomato sauce with eggplant and ricotta salata cheese. In this recipe, I roast the eggplant instead of frying it for easier prep. It's a delicious, satisfying vegetarian dinner!

ingredients: ▢ ¼ teaspoon sea salt, plus more for sprinkling
▢ ½ cup grated ricotta salata or pecorino cheese, plus more for serving
▢ ¼ teaspoon sea salt, plus more for sprinkling
▢ ½ cup grated ricotta salata or pecorino cheese, plus more for serving
https://www.loveandlemons.com/pasta-alla.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
Place the tomatoes and their juices in a large bowl and use your hands to crush them. Set aside.
Halve the eggplants lengthwise, then cut each half into ¼- to ½-inch-thick half-moons. Cut any very large half-moons in half to form wedges.
Divide the eggplant between the two baking sheets. Drizzle each sheet with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil (4 tablespoons total) and sprinkle generously with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and spread evenly on the baking sheets. Roast for 25 to 35 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare the pasta according to the package instructions, cooking until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic, oregano, and red pepper flakes and sizzle for 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste, then add the crushed tomatoes, salt, and several grinds of pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes, or until slightly thickened.
When the pasta is al dente, use a spider or slotted spoon to transfer it from the pot to the skillet with the sauce. Add the roasted eggplant and stir to coat. Add the cheese and stir until melted, adding pasta water as needed to help it melt into the sauce.
Season to taste and serve topped with basil and more cheese, if desired.

ingredients: 16 oz. jarred mild thick and chunky salsa ($1.92**)
15 oz. can black beans (drained and rinsed, $0.92)
16 oz. jarred mild thick and chunky salsa ($1.92**)
15 oz. can black beans (drained and rinsed, $0.92)
https://www.budgetbytes.com/taco-cassero.instructions:
Gather and prepare all ingredients. Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 oven-safe baking dish.
Brown the beef
Heat a medium skillet over medium heat. Once hot, add the ground beef, onions, and green peppers, and sauté for 5 minutes until the meat is browned and the vegetables are tender.
Soak the grease
Using paper towels, carefully soak up the excess grease and discard.
Season the beef
Add the chili powder, cumin, paprika, dried oregano, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the salsa and drained black beans and continue cooking for 4 minutes.
Layer the casserole
To assemble the taco bake, lay two tortillas overlapping each other on the bottom of the baking dish. Top with ⅓ of the meat filling and ⅓ of the cheese. Repeat the layers three times.
Bake and serve
Bake for 20 minutes in the oven until it is melty. Remove them from the oven, slice, and garnish with any toppings you like!

ingredients: 1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into 1-inch pieces)
1 ½ tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (divided)
1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into 1-inch pieces)
1 ½ tablespoons extra virgin olive oil (divided)
https://www.skinnytaste.com/fall-chicken.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425F. Combine all the spices and salt in a small bowl.
Add the veggies to a large mixing bowl. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and season with half of the spices. Mix to evenly combine. Transfer onto a large rimmed sheet pan and spread into an even layer.
Season the chicken with remaining oil and remaining spices. Transfer to the baking sheet in between the veggies in an even layer.
Transfer the baking sheet to the oven and roast for 30-35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Top with feta and broil 2 to 3 minutes, until melted and slightly charred.

https://www.spendwithpennies.com/tuna-ri.description: This easy tuna rice casserole combines tender rice, flaky tuna, peas, and cheddar in a creamy Alfredo sauce. A buttery Panko topping bakes up crisp and golden.

ingredients: 1 cup frozen peas (or green beans, thawed)
¾ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
1 cup frozen peas (or green beans, thawed)
¾ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
https://www.spendwithpennies.com/tuna-ri.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 350°F, and grease a 2-quart baking dish.
In the casserole dish, combine Alfredo sauce, rice, broth, peas, cheese, onion powder, garlic powder, pepper, and celery salt. Stir until well mixed.
Gently fold in the drained tuna. Cover tightly with foil or a lid and bake covered for 30 minutes.

Bake uncovered for an additional 15 to 20 minutes or until hot & bubbly, and the rice is tender. Broil for 1 to 2 minutes for a crisper, more golden top if desired.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-tend.description: These easy Chicken Tenders are oven baked with a crisp panko coating and tender chicken inside, perfect for busy lunches, dinners, or meal prep.
https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-tend.instructions:
Gather and preheat
Gather ingredients. Preheat oven to 400℉.
Combine wet ingredients
Add the chicken, Greek yogurt, salt, and water to a bowl.
Marinate chicken
Mix to combine. Cover the marinating chicken and refrigerate.
Make the panko
In a medium-size mixing bowl, mix together panko, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and neutral oil.
Spread the panko out on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Toast the breadcrumbs
Toast them for 2-5 minutes in the oven until golden brown. It’s ok if the panko varies in color, toasting them before breading helps make these chicken tenders extra crispy, but they will continue to brown on the chicken during the baking process. Set a timer for 2 minutes to start with and check them! The panko can burn fast!
Bread the chicken
Transfer the toasted panko back to the mixing bowl you used to add the seasonings. One at a time, using your hands or tongs, toss the marinated chicken tenders in the toasted panko mixture, pressing it into the panko to make sure they are thoroughly covered on both sides.
Arrange on tray
Transfer each breaded chicken tender to a parchment-lined baking sheet. (You can use the same parchment and baking sheet you toasted the panko crumbs on.)
Bake the chicken tenders in the oven for 30 minutes, flipping them halfway through. Make sure they reach the minimum internal temperature of 165℉.

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/one-pan-pe.description: This easy one-pan pesto orzo recipe is made with Italian chicken sausage, blistered tomatoes, spinach, basil pesto and lemon for a fresh and flavorful weeknight dinner.

ingredients: 12 ounces fully cooked Italian chicken sausage (sliced into ½-inch rounds)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more as needed)
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes (optional)
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth (plus more as needed)
½ cup basil pesto (homemade or store-bought)
optional toppings: fresh basil, grated Parmesan, torn burrata
12 ounces fully cooked Italian chicken sausage (sliced into ½-inch rounds)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more as needed)
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes (optional)
3 cups low-sodium chicken broth (plus more as needed)
½ cup basil pesto (homemade or store-bought)
optional toppings: fresh basil, grated Parmesan, torn burrata
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/one-pan-pe.instructions:
Brown the sausage. Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large sauté pan or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken sausage and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned. Transfer the sausage to a clean plate and set aside.
Blister the tomatoes. Add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet. Add the tomatoes and cook over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring only once or twice, until their skins are blistered and a few tomatoes are just beginning to split. Season with the black pepper, then transfer the tomatoes to the plate with the sausage.
Toast the orzo. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and crushed red pepper flakes and sauté for 30 seconds, stirring constantly. Add the orzo and cook for 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Cook the orzo. Pour in the chicken broth and stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook uncovered for 9 to 11 minutes, stirring frequently, until the orzo is al dente. Add an extra splash of broth as needed if the mixture becomes too dry before the orzo is finished cooking.
Finish the orzo. Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the browned chicken sausage, spinach, pesto and lemon juice until evenly combined and the spinach is wilted, about 1 to 2 minutes. Gently fold in the blistered tomatoes. Add another splash of broth if needed to loosen the sauce.
Serve. Taste and season with additional black pepper as needed. Serve warm with your desired toppings.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/butternut-sq.description: This easy Butternut Squash Lasagna is a cozy vegetarian dinner with roasted squash, mushrooms, kale, cheese, and creamy sage brown butter béchamel.

ingredients: 1 medium butternut squash (halved and seeded, (about 2½-3 pounds) $3.85)
1 medium butternut squash (halved and seeded, (about 2½-3 pounds) $3.85)
https://www.budgetbytes.com/butternut-sq.instructions:
Gather and preheat
Gather and prep all ingredients and preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Roast the squash
Cut your butternut squash in half lengthwise and brush cut sides with olive oil, sprinkle with ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp pepper, and 1 tsp poultry seasoning. Place cut-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet and roast for 40-50 minutes, until tender.
Sauté the veggies
While the squash is roasting, in a large skillet, oil over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic and mushrooms until softened, and mushrooms have released their liquid and browned about 8-10 minutes.
Add kale and cook until wilted and tender. Season with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper. Set aside.
Blend the squash
Scoop squash into a blender or food processor. Add cottage cheese and vegetable broth. Blend until smooth.
Make sage butter
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the sage leaves and swirl the pan as the butter foams and turns golden brown. Watch closely-the aroma should be nutty and toasty. Remove from heat, let cool for a few minutes, then transfer the crispy sage to a paper towel and set aside.
Thicken the sauce
Return the browned butter to medium heat and whisk in the flour, cooking for about a minute to get rid of any raw flavor. Slowly pour in the milk while whisking constantly, then bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Keep whisking until it thickens, about 5-6 minutes (see notes).
Season the sauce
Stir in Parmesan and 1 tsp poultry seasoning into the bechamel. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Assemble the layers
Assemble the butternut squash lasagna: Lightly grease a 9×13 baking dish and spread a thin layer of béchamel on the bottom to prevent sticking. Layer lasagna noodles over the béchamel. Spread a generous layer of squash purée on top. Then add a layer of mushroom-kale mixture, then drizzle with béchamel and sprinkle mozzarella.
Repeat the layers
Then repeat layering: noodles, squash purée, vegetable mixture, béchamel, mozzarella.
Finish the lasagna
Finish with a final layer of noodles, béchamel, and mozzarella.
Bake the lasagna
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly. Let rest at least 10 minutes before slicing.
Slice and serve
Slice the lasagna and serve, topping each portion with the crispy sage leaves.

https://www.spendwithpennies.com/zuppa-t.description: This creamy zuppa Toscana combines Italian sausage, smoky bacon, tender potatoes, and kale in a rich, flavorful broth for an easy one-pot dinner everyone loves.

ingredients: 4 cups potatoes (peeled and cut into ½" cubes)
1 ½ cups kale (chopped, or fresh spinach)
4 cups potatoes (peeled and cut into ½" cubes)
1 ½ cups kale (chopped, or fresh spinach)
https://www.spendwithpennies.com/zuppa-t.instructions:
In a large soup pot or Dutch oven, cook bacon over medium heat until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon to a paper towel-lined plate. Set aside.
Add sausage and onion to the bacon grease and cook until no pink remains. Drain fat.
Add potatoes, kale, chicken broth, garlic, and crushed peppers (if using) to the pot.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer uncovered 12-14 minutes or until potatoes are soft.
Stir in heavy cream and let simmer 1 minute. Taste and season with salt & pepper if desired.
Garnish with bacon.

https://www.spendwithpennies.com/cook-po.description: This pork tenderloin recipe is seared until golden, oven roasted until juicy, and served with an optional creamy mushroom sauce. It is an easy dinner that feels special enough for guests.

ingredients: ½ cup white wine (or chicken broth)
½ cup white wine (or chicken broth)
https://www.spendwithpennies.com/cook-po.instructions:
Pork Tenderloin
Preheat oven to 400° F. Line a baking sheet with foil.
Season the pork with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the tenderloin in the pan, rotating until all sides are golden. Place on prepared baking sheet.
Cook for 18 to 20 minutes or until a thermometer reads an internal temperature of 145℉.
Allow to rest for at least 5 minutes before slicing.
Optional Mushroom Sauce
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and starting to soften.
Add onion and thyme. Reduce heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes more.
Add the wine and Worcestershire to the pan. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring to loosen any bits off the pan, until the liquid has nearly evaporated from the pan.
Add the butter to the pan, stirring to melt. Sprinkle in the flour and stir to coat the mushrooms. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes more.
Gradually whisk in broth and bring to a boil.
Simmer until thickened, about 4 to 5 minutes. Taste and season with salt and pepper as desired. Serve with sliced tenderloin.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-and-.author: Beth Moncel
https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-and-.description: This cozy homemade Chicken and Dumplings recipe features tender chicken thighs simmered in a rich gravy and topped with fluffy dumplings made from scratch.
https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-and-.instructions:
Chicken and Gravy
Brown the chicken
Heat the olive oil in a deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, add the chicken thighs and brown on each side. The chicken does not need to be cooked through at this point, just make sure they get very brown on the outside. Transfer the partially cooked chicken to a clean bowl.
Saute the onion
After removing the chicken from the skillet, add the diced onion and minced garlic and sauté over medium heat until the onions have softened. Stir to dissolve the browned bits off the bottom of the skillet as the onions cook.
Saute the veggies
Add the diced carrot and celery to the skillet with the onion and garlic and continue to sauté for about 5 minutes more.
Make a roux
Add the butter and flour to the skillet and stir until the butter has melted and created a paste with the flour that coats the vegetables. Continue to cook and stir this mixture for about 2 minutes.
Simmer the gravy
Add the parsley, thyme, rosemary, sage, salt, pepper, chicken broth, and milk to the skillet. Turn the heat up to medium-high and continue to stir and cook until the mixture comes up to a simmer and thickens into a gravy.
Add the chicken
Dice the chicken and add it back to the skillet with the vegetables and gravy. Cover with a lid and let the chicken simmer in the gravy over medium heat while you prepare the dumplings.
Dumplings
Mix dry ingredients
To prepare the dumplings, combine the flour, parsley, sugar, salt, baking powder, garlic powder, and pepper in a bowl.
Make the batter
Pour the milk and melted butter into the flour mixture, then stir until a soft, scoopable batter is formed. Do not over stir.
Drop the dumplings
Remove the lid from the chicken and gravy and drop the dumpling batter onto the surface of the gravy in 2 Tbsp dollops. You should get about 12 dumplings.
Simmer and serve
Make sure the gravy is still simmering, then place the lid back on the skillet and allow the dumplings to simmer for 15 minutes. Make sure they're simmering the entire time. After 15 minutes the dumplings should have doubled in size and will be fluffy and cooked in the center. Also, check that the thickest chicken pieces have reached 165°F. Serve hot and enjoy!

ingredients: 1 cup long grain white rice (such as Jasmine or basmati; do not use any other kind of rice)
1 15-ounce can reduced-sodium black beans ( rinsed and drained)
1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese (Colby Jack, or sharp cheddar cheese)
Chopped cilantro (sliced green onion, or a squeeze of lime for serving, optional)
1 cup long grain white rice (such as Jasmine or basmati; do not use any other kind of rice)

https://www.wellplated.com/taco-rice-mea.instructions:
Place a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 375°F. Arrange 4 oven-safe glass meal prep containers (about 3 1/2 cups each) on a rimmed baking sheet. I use these.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Once the skillet is hot, add the oil and let warm for a minute. Add the beef in a single block, then sprinkle with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper. Let brown for a few minutes, then break the meat into crumbles and continue browning until fully cooked through. Taste to adjust the seasoning, then remove from the heat.
To each container, add ¼ cup rice, a scant ½ cup broth (just divide the can 4 ways), ⅓ cup salsa, a scant ½ cup black beans, 1 ½ tablespoons green chiles, and a quarter of the browned beef. Stir until well combined and the rice is fully moistened.
Sprinkle with 1/4 cup cheese and cover with foil. Bake for 35 to 45 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Let cool completely before covering and storing. Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat uncovered in the microwave for about 2 minutes, stirring halfway, or covered in a 350°F oven until warmed through, about 15 minutes. Top with cilantro, green onion, and/or limes prior to serving.

ingredients: 6 boneless skinless chicken breasts (pounded to ½-inch thickness)
½ tablespoon hot sauce (I used Sriracha)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
6 boneless skinless chicken breasts (pounded to ½-inch thickness)
½ tablespoon hot sauce (I used Sriracha)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
https://www.wellplated.com/cornflake-chi.instructions:
Shake
Place the chicken in a large ziptop bag with the buttermilk and hot sauce. Close the bag, turn until the chicken pieces are fully coated, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat
Position a rack in the center of the oven. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Coat a wire rack with nonstick spray and place it on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Dredge
Set up your dredging station: Place the flour on a wide, shallow plate. Set a medium bowl beside it (this will be for the buttermilk). In a separate, wide bowl (a pie dish works well), mix the cornflake crumbs, paprika, salt, black pepper, cayenne, garlic powder, onion powder, and poultry seasoning in a shallow bowl until the ingredients are evenly distributed.
Remove the chicken breasts from the bag and place them on a clean plate. Pour the marinade into the medium bowl.
Dredge each breast with the flour until fully coated, shaking off any excess. Then coat the chicken in the marinade, shaking off any excess. Last, dip it in the cornflake mixture, patting it a bit if needed to help the cornflakes adhere.
Bake
Arrange the chicken pieces on the prepared wire rack. Bake for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F and continue baking until the chicken is cooked through (it should register 155 degrees to 165 degrees F on an instant read thermometer) and crispy, about 15 to 20 minutes more. Let rest 5 minutes, then serve

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/sausag.description: This roasted sausage stuffed butternut squash is filled with Italian sausage, apples, cranberries, kale, pecans and savory fresh herbs. It’s packed with sweet and savory fall flavors and makes a hearty seasonal dinner or beautiful holiday side dish. Paleo, gluten-free and Whole30 friendly.

ingredients: 3 Tbsp avocado oil (or olive oil, divided)
Sea salt and black pepper (to taste)
3 Tbsp avocado oil (or olive oil, divided)
Sea salt and black pepper (to taste)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/sausag.instructions:
Preheat your oven to 425° F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut open each butternut squash lengthwise so you have 4 long halves. Scoop out the seeds and strings, then drizzle with 2 Tbsp of the oil and sprinkle generously with sea salt and pepper. Place face down on the baking sheet and roast in the preheated oven for about 40 minutes, or until softened. Pressing the top of the squash will give you a sense of how soft it is without having to remove it from the oven.
Meanwhile, heat a large skillet over medium heat and add the remaining tablespoon of oil. Crumble the sausage into the skillet and cook until about 3/4 of the way done. Add the onions and garlic and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes until soft and fragrant. Add in the fresh herbs (or dried, if using) and continue to cook for another minute.
Add in the kale, apples, and pecans and cook, stirring to combine flavors, for another minute or two until just softened. Remove from heat, stir in the cranberries, and season the mixture to taste with sea salt and black pepper.
Once the squash is done, allow it to cool for about 5 minutes, then use a spoon to carefully scoop out the flesh, leaving about 3/4” border around the sides and bottom. You can save the squash for another use, or even freeze it to keep longer.
Spoon the sausage mixture into the squash generously to use all of it up. Once filled, place the baking sheet under the broiler and broil until the top of the stuffing and squash are golden brown, 2-4 minutes or so. Garnish with additional fresh herbs if desired and enjoy!

https://fitslowcookerqueen.com/slow-cook.description: Slow cooker lasagna soup has all the comforting flavors of traditional lasagna in an easy, spoonable meal. Ground sausage, tomatoes, vegetables, and broken lasagna noodles cook in a rich, savory broth before each bowl is finished with a creamy combination of ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan cheese. This is a hearty, family-friendly soup that gives you the taste of lasagna without the work of layering and baking a casserole. Instructions for Instant Pot lasagna soup are also included.

ingredients: 6 ounces uncooked lasagna noodles, broken into bite-size pieces
6 ounces uncooked lasagna noodles, broken into bite-size pieces
https://fitslowcookerqueen.com/slow-cook.instructions:
Slow Cooker
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground sausage, onion and garlic. Cook until the beef is browned and no longer pink, crumbling it with a spatula as it cooks. Drain the excess grease. Transfer the sausage mixture to the slow cooker.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, Italian seasoning, fennel seeds, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using). Stir to mix well.
Cook on HIGH for 3 to 4 hours for LOW for 6 to 8 hours.
If the slow cooker is set to LOW, turn it to HIGH. Stir in the broken lasagna noodles during the final 20 to 30 minutes of cooking. Cover and cook until the noodles are tender, stirring once or twice to prevent them from sticking together.
While the noodles cook, combine the ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan in a medium-size bowl.
When the noodles are tender, stir the soup and add more beef broth if you prefer a thinner consistency. Taste and adjust the seasonings as needed.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and top each serving with a generous spoonful of the cheese mixture.
Instant Pot
Set the Instant Pot to sauté. Add the ground sausage and onion. Cook until the sausage is browned and no longer pink, crumbling it as it cooks. Drain any excess grease.
Add the garlic and cook for approximately 1 minute, stirring frequently. Turn off the sauté function.
Pour in the beef broth. Use a wooden spoon to scrape all the browned bits from the bottom of the pot to help prevent a burn notice.
Stir the Italian seasoning, fennel seeds, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes into the broth.
Add the broken lasagna noodles and gently press them into the liquid. Pour the tomato sauce and crushed tomatoes evenly over the top. Do not stir.
Close and seal the lid. Cook on HIGH pressure for 4 minutes.
When the cooking time is complete, carefully quick release the pressure.
Open the lid and stir the soup well, separating any noodles that have stuck together. Let it sit for 5 to 10 minutes; the broth will thicken slightly as it rests. Add more beef broth if you prefer a thinner soup.
Combine the ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan in a separate bowl. Ladle the soup into bowls and top each serving with a generous spoonful of the cheese mixture.

ingredients: ▢ ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil or unsalted butter
▢ ¼ teaspoon sea salt, plus more to taste
▢ Fresh dill or parsley, for garnish
▢ ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil or unsalted butter
▢ ¼ teaspoon sea salt, plus more to taste
▢ Fresh dill or parsley, for garnish
https://www.loveandlemons.com/turkish-eg.instructions:
In a small skillet, combine the olive oil, Aleppo pepper, cumin, and paprika. Place over medium heat and cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until the oil is fragrant and lightly bubbling. Remove from the heat and transfer to a heatproof bowl to prevent burning.
In a medium bowl, stir together the yogurt, garlic, and salt.
Poach the eggs. Crack the eggs into four separate small bowls or ramekins. Bring a medium pot of water to a gentle boil. Add the vinegar and stir the water so that it moves in a circular motion. Use a slotted spoon to scoop the eggs out of the water and transfer to a plate to drain slightly.
Divide the yogurt between two plates or bowls and spread it in a thick swoosh. Top each one with two eggs and drizzle with the Aleppo pepper oil. Season to taste with salt and pepper, garnish with dill or parsley, and serve with pita.

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/chicke.description: This easy Chicken Apple Sausage Sheet Pan Dinner is packed with cozy fall flavors! Chicken apple sausage roasts with tender sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, red onion, and fresh apples, then everything is tossed with a simple maple Dijon sauce. It’s an easy gluten-free and dairy-free dinner that’s perfect for busy fall weeknights.

ingredients: 1 lb fully cooked chicken apple sausage (sliced on a slight diagonal into 3/4- to 1-inch pieces)
1 large sweet potato (peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes, about 3 cups)
2 medium crisp apples (such as SugarBee, Honeycrisp, or Pink Lady, cored and cut into 1-inch chunks)
3 tablespoons avocado oil or olive oil (divided)
3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt (plus more to taste)
1 small garlic clove (finely minced or grated)
1 lb fully cooked chicken apple sausage (sliced on a slight diagonal into 3/4- to 1-inch pieces)
1 large sweet potato (peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes, about 3 cups)

3 tablespoons avocado oil or olive oil (divided)
3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt (plus more to taste)
1 small garlic clove (finely minced or grated)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/chicke.instructions:
Preheat your oven to 425°F. Lightly grease a large rimmed sheet pan. You can line the pan with parchment for easier cleanup, although an unlined metal pan will give you the best browning.
Give the sweet potatoes a head start. Add the sweet potato cubes to the sheet pan. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of the oil and season lightly with salt and pepper. Toss to coat and spread into a single layer and roast for 10 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven and add the Brussels sprouts, red onion, and chicken apple sausage. Drizzle with another 1 tablespoon oil and sprinkle with the garlic powder, thyme, smoked paprika, remaining salt, and black pepper.
Toss everything together and spread into an even layer. Arrange as many sausage pieces as possible with a cut side directly against the sheet pan. Return the pan to the oven and roast for 10 minutes.
While the sausage and vegetables roast, whisk together the Dijon mustard, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, olive oil, garlic, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Remove the pan from the oven and add the cut apples. Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil and about half of the maple Dijon sauce. Toss gently to coat and spread everything back into an even layer.
Return the sheet pan to the oven and roast for another 12–15 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are completely fork-tender, the Brussels sprouts are browned, the apples are tender but still hold their shape, and the sausage is browned around the edges. Drizzle the remaining maple Dijon sauce over everything and serve warm.

Gather and prep ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with foil or parchment.

Serve

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/mexican-ri.instructions:
Rinse the rice. Place the rice in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse under cool running water until the water runs mostly clear. Let it drain for at least 5 minutes, shaking off as much excess water as possible. Blot the bottom of the strainer with a clean kitchen towel to help remove any remaining moisture.
Toast the rice. Heat the oil in a medium saucepan or deep sauté pan over medium heat. Add the drained rice and cook for 4 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the onion, tomato paste and seasonings. Stir in the onion. Continue cooking for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the onion begins to soften and the rice looks opaque with some lightly golden grains. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, cumin, chili powder, salt, oregano and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the tomato paste darkens slightly and smells fragrant.
Add the liquids. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce. Stir well, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom of the pan.
Simmer the rice. Increase the heat to medium-high and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Stir once, cover the pan and reduce the heat to the lowest setting. Cook without lifting the lid or stirring for 15 minutes.
Add the corn. If using frozen corn, quickly lift the lid and scatter it evenly over the rice without stirring. Immediately replace the lid and continue cooking over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes. If using canned corn, continue cooking the rice covered for 3 minutes, then quickly scatter the well-drained corn over the top. Replace the lid and cook for 1 additional minute, just until warmed through.
Rest the rice. Remove the pan from the heat and let the rice rest, still covered, for 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid during this time.
Finish. Remove the lid and let the rice sit uncovered for 2 minutes to allow excess steam to escape. Gently fluff the rice with a fork, then fold in the cilantro and 1 tablespoon lime juice.
Season and serve. Taste and add more lime juice or additional salt if needed. Serve warm and enjoy!

https://www.wellplated.com/gyro-recipe/.description: This sheet pan gyro recipe combines savory meat, warm pita, fresh veggies, and creamy tzatziki. An easy way to make gyros at home!

ingredients: 1 pound lean ground beef (I used 90% lean)
Pita bread (brown rice, white rice, or Lemon Rice)
Tzatziki sauce, plain Greek yogurt, or cottage cheese
Hummus (a fun bonus on the side)
1 pound lean ground beef (I used 90% lean)
Pita bread (brown rice, white rice, or Lemon Rice)
Tzatziki sauce, plain Greek yogurt, or cottage cheese
Hummus (a fun bonus on the side)
https://www.wellplated.com/gyro-recipe/.instructions:
Prepare
Place a rack in the upper third of the oven and preheat to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper (I used an 11x17-inch sheet pan).
Mix
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground lamb, garlic, oregano, cumin, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Turn it out onto the prepared baking sheet. With your fingers, squish it into a thin, even layer that extends nearly to the edges of the paper.
Score
With a bench scraper or butter knife, score the meat lengthwise (hot dog style) down the center, then crosswise into 1-inch strips. Lightly brush the top with oil (I drizzled a bit on, then used a pastry brush to spread it).
Bake
Place in the oven on the upper-third rack and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the meat is cooked through and beginning to brown on top. It will release a good amount of liquid and some grease, but don’t be alarmed—it’s going to taste great.
Drain
Remove the pan from the oven and carefully pour off the excess liquid. With a bench scraper or knife, separate the meat back into strips (it will have fused along the score lines as the meat cooked).
Assemble
Warm the pita in the microwave, or place it on a lower oven rack for a minute or two. Load up your gyro with tzatziki, strips of the cooked gyro meat, and your toppings of choice. Enjoy warm.

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/chicken-ba.instructions:
Cook the bacon. Add the bacon to a large sauté pan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until browned and crisp. Transfer the bacon to a paper-towel-lined plate using a slotted spoon. Leave about 1 tablespoon of bacon grease in the pan and reserve the rest.
Sauté the vegetables. Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the white parts of the scallions, bell pepper and jalapeño to the pan. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring frequently. Transfer the vegetables to a large mixing bowl.
Cook the chicken. Toss the chicken with 2 tablespoons of the taco seasoning until evenly coated. Add 1 tablespoon of the reserved bacon grease (or oil) to the same pan, then add the chicken in an even layer. Cook over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Transfer the chicken to the bowl with the vegetables.
Add the beans and seasonings. Add the cooked bacon, beans, corn and remaining 1 tablespoon taco seasoning to the bowl. Toss until everything is evenly combined.
Finish the filling. Add the green parts of the scallions, cilantro, sour cream and 2 tablespoons lime juice. Stir until evenly combined.
Taste and season. Taste the filling before assembling the quesadillas. Add fine sea salt, freshly ground black pepper, additional lime juice or a little more taco seasoning as needed. The filling should taste well seasoned on its own, since the tortillas and cheese will soften the flavors slightly.
Assemble the quesadillas. Place a tortilla on a clean work surface. Sprinkle ¼ cup of the cheese over one half of the tortilla. Top with a heaping ½ cup of the chicken filling, spreading it in an even layer, then sprinkle with another ¼ cup cheese. Fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling and press gently to flatten. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, filling and cheese.
Cook the quesadillas. Heat a large nonstick or cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Lightly brush the skillet with oil. Cook the quesadillas one or two at a time for 2 to 4 minutes per side, pressing gently with a spatula, until the tortillas are crisp and golden and the cheese has completely melted.
Wipe down the skillet. Between batches, carefully wipe the skillet clean with a dry paper towel to remove any stray cheese or filling that could burn. Add another light coating of oil before cooking the next batch. Reduce the heat as needed if the tortillas begin browning before the cheese melts.
Serve. Let the quesadillas rest for 2 minutes, then cut each one into wedges. Serve warm with your favorite toppings and sauces.

ingredients: 1 lb Sweet or spicy Italian sausage meat (homemade* or store bought)
2 large Russet potatoes (about 1.5 lbs, peeled and cut into 1/2” cubes*)
Sea Salt and pepper to taste
1 lb Sweet or spicy Italian sausage meat (homemade* or store bought)

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/zuppa-.instructions:
Heat a large stock pot (cast iron is ideal) over medium high heat. Add the bacon pieces and cook, stirring occasionally to evenly brown, until crisp - about 5-8 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked bacon to a paper-towel lined plate to drain.
Lower the heat to medium and save the bacon fat in the pot. Add the sausage to the pot and sprinkle with crushed red pepper, if desired. Cook, stirring and breaking up lumps with a spoon, until browed - about 5-8 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to remove the sausage to a plate to drain. Save the fat in the pot.
With the heat still over medium, add the onions to the pot and cook until translucent, then add the garlic, stir, and cook another 45 seconds. Add the potatoes to the pot, sprinkle the potatoes, onions, and garlic with sea salt and pepper and stir to coat.
Add the broth to the pot and bring to a boil over medium high heat. Lower the heat to medium and continue to cook until potatoes are fork tender - about 10 minutes. If using mushrooms or cauliflower**, move on to the next step after the broth boils.
Add the coconut milk to the pot and the sausage, stir cook about 5 minutes to blend flavors. Stir in the kale and cooked bacon, cooking just another minute or so until the kale is wilted and vibrant green. Season the soup with sea salt and pepper to taste, if desired.
Remove from heat and serve - the soup will thicken as it cools. This soup stores well covered in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, or, you can freeze it for up to one month. Enjoy!

ingredients: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 large yellow onion (halved and thinly sliced)
2 tablespoons ghee (avocado oil or olive oil)
1 pound mild or sweet Italian sausage (casings removed if necessary)
1 medium-large firm apple (cored and diced into ½-inch pieces)
Additional salt and black pepper (as needed)

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/sausag.instructions:
Preheat your oven to 400°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. Carefully cut each acorn squash in half lengthwise. Use a spoon to scoop out the seeds and stringy pulp.
Brush the cut sides of the squash with the avocado or olive oil and season lightly with salt and black pepper. Place the squash halves cut-side down on the prepared baking sheet.
Roast for 30–40 minutes, depending on the size of the squash, or until the flesh is tender and can be easily pierced with a fork.
While the squash roasts, prepare the filling. Heat the ghee or oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add the sliced onion and a pinch of salt. Cook the onion for 20–25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until very soft and deep golden brown. Reduce the heat if it begins browning too quickly. If necessary, add a tablespoon of water to loosen any browned pieces from the skillet.
Increase the heat to medium and add the sausage to the skillet. Cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles, until browned and no longer pink.

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/paleo-.description: This easy one-pot pumpkin chili combines ground beef and pork with pumpkin, tomatoes, vegetables, and smoky spices. It’s a hearty, comforting dinner that’s paleo, Whole30 compatible, dairy free, and naturally gluten free.

ingredients: ½ pound ground pork (or an additional ½ pound ground beef)
½ tablespoon avocado oil (or olive oil)
1 teaspoon fine sea salt (divided, plus more to taste)
1 jalapeño pepper (seeded if desired and minced)
1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes (undrained, preferably no salt added)
¼ teaspoon chipotle powder (or up to ½ teaspoon for more heat)
Sliced avocado (diced red onion, lime wedges, or dairy-free sour cream, for serving)
½ pound ground pork (or an additional ½ pound ground beef)
½ tablespoon avocado oil (or olive oil)
1 teaspoon fine sea salt (divided, plus more to taste)
1 jalapeño pepper (seeded if desired and minced)
1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes (undrained, preferably no salt added)
¼ teaspoon chipotle powder (or up to ½ teaspoon for more heat)
Sliced avocado (diced red onion, lime wedges, or dairy-free sour cream, for serving)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/paleo-.instructions:
Stovetop Instructions:
Heat a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the avocado oil.
Add the ground beef and pork. Season with ½ teaspoon of the salt and black pepper. Cook, breaking the meat apart with a wooden spoon, until it is about two-thirds browned.
Drain off some of the excess fat if necessary, leaving a small amount in the pot for flavor. Add the onion and green bell pepper. Cook for three to four minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat is completely browned and the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the garlic and jalapeño. Cook for one minute, stirring frequently.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, undrained diced tomatoes, pumpkin puree, remaining ½ teaspoon salt, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, chipotle powder, and pumpkin pie spice.
Bring the chili to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat to a slow simmer and partially cover the pot. Simmer for at least 15 minutes or up to 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. For thicker chili, uncover the pot during the final 5–10 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt and seasonings. Serve topped with cilantro, avocado, diced red onion, lime, or dairy-free sour cream, if desired.
Slow Cooker Instructions:
Follow Steps 1–4 above to brown the meat and cook the vegetables.
Transfer the meat and vegetable mixture to a slow cooker. Add the crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, pumpkin puree, remaining salt, and all the spices. Stir to combine.
Cover and cook on low for four hours.
Stir well, taste, and adjust the seasonings before serving with your favorite toppings.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-stew.description: This chicken stew is a rich and hearty mix of tender chicken thighs, vegetables, and a light but flavorful herb-infused gravy.

ingredients: ½ lb. carrots (thinly sliced,(3 carrots, about 1.5 cups) $0.57)
1¾ lbs. chicken thighs (boneless & skinless, cut into 1-inch pieces (about 6 thighs) $5.64*)
1½ lbs. baby potatoes (cut in half (cubed Yukon also work) $3.74)
½ lb. carrots (thinly sliced,(3 carrots, about 1.5 cups) $0.57)
1¾ lbs. chicken thighs (boneless & skinless, cut into 1-inch pieces (about 6 thighs) $5.64*)
1½ lbs. baby potatoes (cut in half (cubed Yukon also work) $3.74)
https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-stew.instructions:
Gather and prepare all ingredients.
Prep the fresh ingredients
Dice the onion and celery, mince the garlic, slice the carrots, and cut the baby potatoes in half before you begin.
Cut and coat chicken
Cut the chicken thighs into 1-inch pieces. Add them to a large bowl and sprinkle 2 Tbsp flour over the chicken. Toss until the chicken is evenly coated. (See browning note).
Heat butter and oil
Add the butter and olive oil to a large pot. Heat the butter and oil over medium until they are hot and sizzling. (See browning note).
Brown the chicken
Add the flour-coated chicken to the pot and allow the chicken to brown on all sides (avoid stirring until browned on the bottom) for about 5 minutes on each side. When the chicken is browned and there is a nice brown layer of flour on the bottom of the pot, remove the chicken to a clean bowl with a slotted spoon. The chicken does not need to be cooked through at this point, just browned on the outside.
Saute the veggies
Add the onion, celery, garlic, and carrots to the pot and continue to sauté until the onions are soft, for about 5 minutes. Use the moisture released by the vegetables to dissolve and scrape the browned bits off the bottom of the pot.
Coat the veggies
Once the vegetables are slightly softened, add the remaining 2 Tbsp flour to the pot and continue to sauté over medium for about two minutes more. The flour will begin to coat the bottom of the pot again.
Add chicken, potatoes and herbs
Return the browned chicken to the pot. Also add the potatoes, dried parsley, thyme, rosemary, sage, salt, and pepper
Add broths to pot
Next, add the chicken broth and vegetable broth. Stir to combine and dissolve any flour off the bottom of the pot.
Simmer the stew
Place a lid on the pot and allow it to come up to a boil. Once it reaches a boil, remove the lid and turn the heat down to medium-low. Allow the stew to simmer over medium-low, without a lid and stirring occasionally, for about 30 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and the broth has thickened.
Taste and serve
Taste the stew and add salt if needed (I didn't add any additional salt, but it'll depend on the salt content of the broth you used). Add a tablespoon of fresh chopped parsley if desired, and serve hot.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/creamy-butte.description: This Creamy Butternut Squash Orzo is an easy one-pot dinner with tender squash, kale, Parmesan, and a rich, creamy sauce. Ready in under an hour!

ingredients: 1 butternut squash (peeled, tipped, seeds removed & small dice, (about 2 lbs. - heaping 4 cups) $3.08*)
1 small bunch kale (washed, stripped, & chopped (2 cups pressed) $1.24****)
1 butternut squash (peeled, tipped, seeds removed & small dice, (about 2 lbs. - heaping 4 cups) $3.08*)
1 small bunch kale (washed, stripped, & chopped (2 cups pressed) $1.24****)
https://www.budgetbytes.com/creamy-butte.instructions:
Prep the butternut squash
Gather and prepare all ingredients. Peel the butternut squash, cut off the ends, and cut the squash in half where the narrow neck meets the bulbous base. Slice the bulbous base in half lengthwise, scoop out the seeds, then cut both the neck and the seeded portion into small-sized cubes.
Brown the squash
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, add the cubed butternut squash in an even layer. Cook for about 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the squash is tender and nicely browned on several sides.
Saute the aromatics
After 15 minutes, add the diced onions, garlic, ½ teaspoon of salt, and ½ teaspoon of pepper. Sauté for about 3 minutes until the onions are softened.
Combine orzo and broth
Add the orzo pasta, vegetable broth, and remaining salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Cook the orzo
Bring the pot to a boil, then reduce to a medium simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring constantly to help break down the squash and orzo. This will help make it thick and creamy.
Add the kale and cream
After 10 minutes, add the cinnamon, chopped kale, and heavy cream. Stir until the kale has wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Garish and serve
Divide the butternut squash orzo into bowls, sprinkle on the fresh Parmesan, and enjoy.

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/creamy.description: This creamy chicken potato casserole is made with tender roasted potatoes, cooked chicken and crispy bacon in a rich, savory dairy-free sauce. It’s family friendly, gluten free, paleo and Whole30 compatible.

ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes (peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes)
1 tablespoon avocado oil or olive oil
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons rendered bacon fat or ghee
1 1/2 cups chicken broth (or chicken bone broth)
1 cup full-fat canned coconut milk (stirred well)
3 cups cooked chicken (roughly chopped or shredded)
Sliced chives or green onions (for garnish)
1 1/2 pounds russet potatoes (peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes)
1 tablespoon avocado oil or olive oil
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 tablespoons rendered bacon fat or ghee
1 1/2 cups chicken broth (or chicken bone broth)
1 cup full-fat canned coconut milk (stirred well)
3 cups cooked chicken (roughly chopped or shredded)
Sliced chives or green onions (for garnish)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/creamy.instructions:
Preheat your oven to 425°F. Place the potatoes in a 9-by-13-inch casserole dish and toss with the oil, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper. Spread the potatoes into an even layer.
Roast the potatoes for about 35 minutes, or until easily pierced with a fork but still holding their shape. Stir once halfway through cooking if desired. When the potatoes are done, reduce the oven temperature to 375°F.
While the potatoes roast, heat a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the bacon until crisp, then transfer it to a paper-towel-lined plate. Reserve three tablespoons of rendered bacon fat for the sauce. If necessary, use ghee in place of some or all of the bacon fat.
Wipe any dark or burned bits from the skillet and return it to medium heat. Add the reserved bacon fat or ghee. Add the onion and cook for three to four minutes, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for about one minute, stirring frequently.
Sprinkle the arrowroot or tapioca starch over the onion mixture and stir for about 30 seconds.
Slowly pour in the chicken broth while whisking, followed by the coconut milk, mustard and nutritional yeast, if using. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer while continuing to whisk. Cook for one to two minutes, until the sauce thickens enough to lightly coat the back of a spoon. Taste and season with salt and black pepper as needed.
Add the cooked chicken to the roasted potatoes and gently toss to combine. Pour the sauce over the chicken and potatoes and stir gently until everything is evenly coated. Crumble the bacon. Stir half of it into the casserole and sprinkle the remaining bacon over the top.
Bake at 375°F for 10–15 minutes, or until the casserole is hot and bubbling around the edges. Garnish with sliced chives or green onions and serve hot. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to four days.

ingredients: 1 cup (200 g) packed light brown sugar
3/4 cup neutral-flavored oil (such as avocado, canola or vegetable oil)
1 cup (200 g) packed light brown sugar
3/4 cup neutral-flavored oil (such as avocado, canola or vegetable oil)
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/pumpkin-sh.instructions:
Prep the oven and pan. Heat oven to 350°F. Grease a 13 x 18-inch rimmed half-sheet pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
Mix the dry ingredients. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, pumpkin pie spice, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda and salt until evenly combined.
Mix the wet ingredients. In a large mixing bowl, whisk the brown sugar, granulated sugar and eggs together for about 30 seconds, until smooth and slightly lightened. Add the pumpkin, oil and vanilla and whisk until completely combined.
Combine. Add the dry ingredients to the pumpkin mixture and gently fold with a rubber spatula just until no streaks of flour remain. Avoid overmixing.
Bake. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread it into an even layer. Bake for 18–23 minutes, or until the center springs back lightly when touched and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs attached.
Cool. Transfer the pan to a wire rack and let the cake cool completely before frosting.
Make the cream cheese frosting. Beat the butter with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until smooth and creamy, about 1 minute. Add the powdered sugar, vanilla and salt and beat on low speed until incorporated, then increase to medium-high and beat until light and fluffy. Add the cream cheese and beat on low speed just until completely combined and smooth. Avoid overmixing, which can make cream cheese frosting runny.
Frost. Spread the cream cheese frosting evenly over the cooled cake. Sprinkle with an extra pinch of pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon, if desired.
Serve. Slice into squares and serve immediately, or refrigerate until ready to serve.

https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/phill.description: These easy Philly cheesesteaks are made with thinly sliced ribeye steak, sautéed onions and green bell peppers, melty provolone cheese, and buttery toasted hoagie rolls. They are hearty, flavorful, and ready in just 30 minutes!

ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless ribeye steak, (or thinly shaved steak)
1 green bell pepper, (seeds removed and thinly sliced)
8 slices provolone cheese, (can use white American cheese)
1 1/2 pounds boneless ribeye steak, (or thinly shaved steak)
1 green bell pepper, (seeds removed and thinly sliced)
8 slices provolone cheese, (can use white American cheese)
https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/phill.instructions:
Thinly slice the steak. For easier slicing, place the ribeye in the freezer for 30 to 45 minutes before slicing. Use a sharp knife to slice the steak as thinly as possible against the grain. Some grocery stores sell thinly shaved steak, which you can use instead of slicing the ribeye yourself.
Cook the onions and peppers. Heat a large skillet (or griddle) over medium heat. Add the olive oil, onion, and green bell pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and lightly golden, about 7 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Toast the rolls. Spread the cut sides of the hoagie rolls with butter. Place them cut-side down in the skillet and toast until lightly golden and crisp. Remove from the skillet.
Cook the steak. Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the thinly sliced ribeye to the hot skillet, spreading it into an even layer. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then toss and continue cooking until browned and cooked through. Season with the salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Chop and add the vegetables. Return the onions and peppers to the skillet. Using a spatula or two sturdy spatulas, chop the steak and vegetables into smaller pieces while tossing them together. Divide the mixture into 4 portions.
Melt the cheese. Top each portion with 2 slices of provolone. Let the cheese melt over the hot steak and vegetables, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Assemble. Use a spatula to scoop each cheesy portion directly into a toasted, buttered hoagie roll. Serve immediately.

ingredients: 1 butternut squash (peeled, tipped, seeds removed & small dice, (about 2 lbs.) $3.08)

https://www.budgetbytes.com/sheet-pan-ch.instructions:
Preheat and prep
Preheat the oven to 450°F. Gather all ingredients and cut all the vegetables.
Season the veggies
For the vegetables, place the cut butternut squash, red onions, and Brussels sprouts in a large bowl. Drizzle in the 2 Tbsp vegetable oil and sprinkle with 1½ tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp garlic powder, and ½ tsp dried thyme. Toss to coat and lay them flat on the sheet pan.
Mix chicken seasoning
For the chicken thighs, in a small bowl, mix the 2 Tbsp vegetable oil, ½ tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp garlic powder, ¼ tsp chili powder, ¼ tsp cinnamon, ¼ tsp dried thyme, 1½ tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper.
Season the chicken
Using a pastry brush, completely coat all sides of the chicken thighs, including underneath the skin. Make sure to distribute the seasoning evenly.

Cook chicken and vegetables
Place the sheet pan in the preheated oven and cook for 30-35 minutes, until the chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 165°F.
Divide and serve
Remove the pan from the oven and divide the vegetables and chicken thighs evenly between five plates, then enjoy.

https://www.wellplated.com/taco-pie/.description: Taco pie layers a tortilla crust with seasoned beef, bell peppers and a creamy, cheesy filling. It’s an easy, satisfying twist on taco night!

ingredients: 3 10-inch flour tortillas (burrito size (I used low carb))
1 small yellow onion (cut into ¼-inch dice)
1 green bell pepper (cut into ¼-inch dice)
1 red bell pepper (cut into ¼-inch dice)
⅓ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt (at room temperature, plus additional for serving)
1 ½ cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese or pepper Jack cheese (6 ounces, divided)
Sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
Sliced green onion or chopped cilantro
3 10-inch flour tortillas (burrito size (I used low carb))
1 small yellow onion (cut into ¼-inch dice)
1 green bell pepper (cut into ¼-inch dice)
1 red bell pepper (cut into ¼-inch dice)
⅓ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt (at room temperature, plus additional for serving)
1 ½ cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese or pepper Jack cheese (6 ounces, divided)
Sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
Sliced green onion or chopped cilantro
https://www.wellplated.com/taco-pie/.instructions:
Prepare
Place a rack in the center of your oven and preheat to 375°F. Lightly coat a 9-inch deep dish pie plate with nonstick spray. If the tortillas feel stiff, warm them in the microwave for 15 seconds so they bend easily without cracking.
Bake
Lay the tortillas into the pie plate, overlapping them across the center so that the edges of the tortillas slightly extend over the top of the plate like the sides of a pie crust. Pleat the edges to flatten them along the edge of the plate. Mist all over with nonstick spray and bake 5 minutes. Set aside.
Soften
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Cook, stirring, until softened, 8 to 10 minutes.
Brown
Add the beef and cook, breaking it into small crumbles. Add the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt, black pepper, cayenne, and green chiles. Stir and continue to break apart the meat until it is fully cooked through and no pink remains.
Cool
Transfer the beef mixture to a large bowl and let it cool 10 minutes, stirring once or twice to release heat from the bottom of the bowl.
Mix
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, Greek yogurt, and hot sauce together until completely smooth with no white streaks. Pour over the cooled beef, add 1 cup of the shredded cheese, and fold until everything is evenly combined.
Assemble
Spread the filling into the tortilla crust, smoothing the top into an even layer. Sprinkle with the remaining ½ cup cheese. With foil strips or a pie crust shield, tend the edges of the tortilla so it doesn't overbrown.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is set (use a butter knife to peek into the center. It should look moist but you shouldn't see liquid pooling).
Rest
Let the taco pie rest 10 minutes. Use a long knife with a sharp, pointy tip to slice (it takes a bit of elbow grease to get through the tortillas). Or for easier slicing, use a large spatula to gently and carefully slide the pie out onto a cutting board, then slice with a chef's knife. Serve with a generous amount of your toppings of choice

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/smoky-ando.description: This smoky andouille lentil soup combines sausage, tender lentils, fire-roasted tomatoes and kale in a hearty broth finished with fresh lemon.

ingredients: 12 ounces andouille smoked sausage (thinly sliced on the diagonal)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more to taste)
1½ cups green or brown lentils (rinsed and picked over)
1 to 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (to taste)
optional toppings: chopped fresh parsley, extra black pepper and/or crushed red pepper flakes
12 ounces andouille smoked sausage (thinly sliced on the diagonal)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more to taste)
1½ cups green or brown lentils (rinsed and picked over)
1 to 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (to taste)
optional toppings: chopped fresh parsley, extra black pepper and/or crushed red pepper flakes
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/smoky-ando.instructions:
Brown the sausage. Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned. Transfer to a clean plate and set aside.
Sauté the vegetables. Add the onion, carrots and celery to the same pot and sauté for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened. Add the garlic, smoked paprika, thyme and black pepper and sauté for 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Simmer. Add the lentils, fire-roasted tomatoes, chicken stock and bay leaf and stir to combine. Bring the soup to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low, partially cover, and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender.
Finish. Return the sausage to the pot and stir in the kale. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the kale is tender and the sausage is warmed through. Remove and discard the bay leaf. Stir in 1 tablespoon lemon juice, then taste and season with salt, additional black pepper and more lemon juice as needed.
Serve. Serve warm, topped with parsley, extra black pepper and/or crushed red pepper flakes if desired.

https://www.spendwithpennies.com/easy-ho.description: This homemade lasagna recipe is delicious and easy to make. It features layers of pasta, meat sauce, and cheese with a golden cheesy topping!
https://www.spendwithpennies.com/easy-ho.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the lasagna noodles and cook until al dente (firm) according to package directions. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet or Dutch oven, brown the beef, sausage, onion, and garlic over medium-high heat until no pink remains. Drain any fat.
Stir in the pasta sauce, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, ½ teaspoon of salt, and ¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 5 minutes or until slightly thickened. Taste and season with additional salt if desired.
In a separate medium bowl, combine 1 ½ cups mozzarella cheese, ¼ cup parmesan cheese, ricotta, parsley, egg, and ¼ teaspoon salt.
Spread 1 cup of the meat sauce in a 9x13 pan or casserole dish. Top it with 3 lasagna noodles. Layer with 1 cup of the ricotta cheese mixture and 1 cup of meat sauce. Repeat twice more. Finish with 3 noodles topped with remaining sauce.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Remove the foil and sprinkle the top of the lasagna with 2 ½ cups mozzarella cheese and ¼ cup Parmesan cheese. Bake uncovered for an additional 15 minutes or until browned and bubbly. Broil for 2-3 minutes if desired.
Rest for at least 15 minutes before cutting.

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/slow-c.description: This creamy white chicken chili is made with tender chicken thighs, white sweet potatoes, green chiles, warming spices and coconut cream. Make it on the stovetop, in the slow cooker or in the Instant Pot for an easy, hearty paleo and Whole30 meal.

ingredients: 1 large white or Japanese sweet potato (peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes, about 3 cups)
1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh jalapeño (more or less to taste)
1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional and to taste)
1 teaspoon sea salt (plus more to taste)
1 1/2 pounds boneless (skinless chicken thighs or chicken breasts)
3 cups chicken broth (for the stovetop method, or 2 cups for the slow cooker or Instant Pot)
1/3 cup coconut cream (plus more as desired)
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice (plus more to taste)
Fresh cilantro (sliced avocado, green onions, jalapeños and lime wedges, for serving)
1 large white or Japanese sweet potato (peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes, about 3 cups)
1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh jalapeño (more or less to taste)
1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional and to taste)
1 teaspoon sea salt (plus more to taste)
1 1/2 pounds boneless (skinless chicken thighs or chicken breasts)
3 cups chicken broth (for the stovetop method, or 2 cups for the slow cooker or Instant Pot)
1/3 cup coconut cream (plus more as desired)
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice (plus more to taste)
Fresh cilantro (sliced avocado, green onions, jalapeños and lime wedges, for serving)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/slow-c.instructions:
Stovetop Instructions:
Heat the avocado oil or ghee in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 2–3 minutes, until it begins to soften. Add the sweet potato and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, cayenne, salt and black pepper. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the green chiles and 3 cups of chicken broth. Stir, then nestle the chicken thighs into the liquid.
Bring the chili to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat to maintain a simmer and partially cover the Dutch oven. Cook for 20–25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are fork-tender and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a plate or cutting board and shred it using two forks.
Mash some of the sweet potatoes against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon or potato masher. Alternatively, use an immersion blender to blend the chili very briefly, leaving plenty of the sweet potato pieces whole.
Stir in the coconut cream, nutritional yeast and lime juice. Return the shredded chicken to the pot and simmer uncovered for 3–5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt, lime juice and coconut cream as desired. Serve hot with cilantro, avocado, green onions, sliced jalapeño and lime wedges.
Slow Cooker Instructions:
Place the sweet potatoes, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, cayenne, salt, black pepper and green chiles in a 6-quart slow cooker.
Arrange the chicken over the vegetables and pour in 2 cups of chicken broth. Cover and cook on low for 5–6 hours or on high for 3–4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the sweet potatoes are tender. Chicken breasts may cook more quickly, so begin checking them early.
Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Mash some of the sweet potatoes directly in the slow cooker to thicken the broth.
Stir in the coconut cream, nutritional yeast and lime juice. Return the shredded chicken to the slow cooker. Cover and cook on high for another 10–15 minutes. Taste, adjust the seasonings and serve with your desired toppings.
Instant Pot Instructions:
Select the sauté function on a 6-quart Instant Pot. Add the avocado oil or ghee, followed by the onion. Cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add the sweet potato and cook for another 2–3 minutes. Stir in the garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, cayenne, salt and black pepper. Cook for 30–60 seconds.
Press cancel. Pour in 2 cups of chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pot thoroughly with a wooden spoon. Stir in the green chiles, then place the chicken on top. Secure the lid and set the pressure valve to sealing. Pressure cook on high for 8 minutes.
When the cooking time is complete, allow the pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully release the remaining pressure.
Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Mash some of the sweet potatoes or briefly blend part of the chili with an immersion blender.
Stir in the coconut cream, nutritional yeast and lime juice. Return the chicken to the pot. If desired, select sauté and simmer for 2–3 minutes to thicken. Taste, adjust the seasonings and serve with your desired toppings.
instructions_list: Stovetop Instructions:

Heat the avocado oil or ghee in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 2–3 minutes, until it begins to soften. Add the sweet potato and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, cayenne, salt and black pepper. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the green chiles and 3 cups of chicken broth. Stir, then nestle the chicken thighs into the liquid.

Bring the chili to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat to maintain a simmer and partially cover the Dutch oven. Cook for 20–25 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are fork-tender and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a plate or cutting board and shred it using two forks.

Mash some of the sweet potatoes against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon or potato masher. Alternatively, use an immersion blender to blend the chili very briefly, leaving plenty of the sweet potato pieces whole.

Stir in the coconut cream, nutritional yeast and lime juice. Return the shredded chicken to the pot and simmer uncovered for 3–5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt, lime juice and coconut cream as desired. Serve hot with cilantro, avocado, green onions, sliced jalapeño and lime wedges.
Slow Cooker Instructions:
Place the sweet potatoes, onion, garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, cayenne, salt, black pepper and green chiles in a 6-quart slow cooker.

Arrange the chicken over the vegetables and pour in 2 cups of chicken broth. Cover and cook on low for 5–6 hours or on high for 3–4 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the sweet potatoes are tender. Chicken breasts may cook more quickly, so begin checking them early.
Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Mash some of the sweet potatoes directly in the slow cooker to thicken the broth.

Stir in the coconut cream, nutritional yeast and lime juice. Return the shredded chicken to the slow cooker. Cover and cook on high for another 10–15 minutes. Taste, adjust the seasonings and serve with your desired toppings.
Instant Pot Instructions:
Select the sauté function on a 6-quart Instant Pot. Add the avocado oil or ghee, followed by the onion. Cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add the sweet potato and cook for another 2–3 minutes. Stir in the garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, cayenne, salt and black pepper. Cook for 30–60 seconds.

Press cancel. Pour in 2 cups of chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pot thoroughly with a wooden spoon. Stir in the green chiles, then place the chicken on top. Secure the lid and set the pressure valve to sealing. Pressure cook on high for 8 minutes.
When the cooking time is complete, allow the pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully release the remaining pressure.
Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Mash some of the sweet potatoes or briefly blend part of the chili with an immersion blender.

Stir in the coconut cream, nutritional yeast and lime juice. Return the chicken to the pot. If desired, select sauté and simmer for 2–3 minutes to thicken. Taste, adjust the seasonings and serve with your desired toppings.

ingredients: 1 teaspoon sea salt (divided plus more to taste)
½ teaspoon black pepper (plus more to taste)
Sliced banana peppers or pickled peppers (optional)
1 teaspoon sea salt (divided plus more to taste)
½ teaspoon black pepper (plus more to taste)

https://www.eatingbirdfood.com/philly-ch.instructions:
Saute veggies
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the olive oil, then add the onion, bell peppers and mushrooms. Season with ½ teaspoon salt and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly caramelized. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Transfer the vegetables to a plate.
Make sauce
While the vegetables are cooking, make the cheese sauce. Add the cottage cheese, cheddar, 1 Tablespoon milk, Dijon mustard, garlic powder and pepper to a high-powered blender and blend until completely smooth. Add an additional tablespoon of milk if the mixture is too thick. Set aside. The sauce is ready to drizzle as is, but if you prefer it warm, heat it gently in a small saucepan over low heat for a few minutes, stirring often. I didn’t find that necessary since the beef and veggies warm it up in the bowl.
Cook beef
Add the ground beef to the same skillet as the veggies and cook, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, until browned and cooked through, about 6–8 minutes. Drain any excess grease, if needed.
Add 2 Tablespoons water or broth to the skillet, followed by the Worcestershire sauce, apple cider vinegar, garlic powder, ½ teaspoon salt, smoked paprika and black pepper. Stir to combine, adding another 1–2 Tablespoons water or broth if the mixture seems dry.
Combine
Return the cooked vegetables to the skillet and toss until everything is well combined and warmed through.
Melt cheese
Reduce the heat to low. Lay the provolone slices evenly over the beef and vegetable mixture. Cover and cook for 1–2 minutes, or until the cheese is melted.
Serve
Divide rice or cauliflower rice among bowls and top with the cheesesteak mixture. Drizzle with the cheese sauce and top with banana peppers and red pepper flakes, if desired.
