https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/huevos-ran.description: This huevos rancheros recipe features corn tortillas layered with refried black beans, fried eggs and a smoky fresh ranchero sauce.

ingredients: 2–3 serrano or jalapeño peppers (stemmed (remove seeds for less heat))
fine sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
Toppings: crumbled cotija or queso fresco (sliced avocado, fresh cilantro, pickled red onions, lime wedges and/or hot sauce)
2–3 serrano or jalapeño peppers (stemmed (remove seeds for less heat))
fine sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper
Toppings: crumbled cotija or queso fresco (sliced avocado, fresh cilantro, pickled red onions, lime wedges and/or hot sauce)
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/huevos-ran.instructions:
Make the fresh ranchero sauce. Preheat your broiler to high (or heat a dry skillet over medium-high). Place the Roma tomatoes, onion half, chile, and unpeeled garlic cloves on a sheet pan. Broil for 8–12 minutes, turning once or twice, until the tomatoes are softened and blistered and the vegetables are nicely charred in spots. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly. Peel the garlic. Transfer everything to a blender along with the chipotle powder, lime juice, and a generous pinch of fine sea salt. Blend until smooth (or leave slightly chunky if you prefer texture). Taste and adjust salt as needed. Set aside.
Make the refried black beans. Heat the oil (or butter or lard) in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the drained black beans, cumin, and a good pinch of salt. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally. Mash the beans to your desired consistency using a potato masher or the back of a spoon. If they seem dry, add a splash of water to loosen. Stir in the lime juice and adjust salt to taste. Keep warm over low heat.
Crisp the tortillas. Heat a thin layer of neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry each corn tortilla for about 30–60 seconds per side until lightly crisped but still flexible. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. (You can also warm them in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame for a lighter option.)
Cook the eggs. In the same skillet, fry the eggs to your liking. Sunny-side up or over-easy are classic for runny yolks. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Assemble. Spread a generous layer of warm refried black beans over each tortilla. Spoon some warm ranchero sauce on top. Add a fried egg to each tortilla (use one or two per serving depending on appetite), then spoon additional sauce over the egg.
Finish and serve. Top with your favorite garnishes and serve immediately while everything is warm and the yolks are beautifully runny.

https://www.skinnytaste.com/bacon-wrappe.description: Juicy bacon-wrapped pork tenderloin with delicata squash, onions, and pears tossed in maple syrup and whole-grain mustard. The smoky bacon, caramelized pears, and tangy mustard make this sheet pan dinner full of fall flavor.

ingredients: 2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard (divided (check label for GF))
2 delicata squash (about 14 oz each, seeded and cut ½-inch thick)
1 large Bartlett pear (ripe, about 8 ounces, cored and cut into 8 wedges (about ¾-inch thick))
1 small red onion (about 8 ounces, cut into 16 wedges (about ½-inch thick))
2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard (divided (check label for GF))
2 delicata squash (about 14 oz each, seeded and cut ½-inch thick)
1 large Bartlett pear (ripe, about 8 ounces, cored and cut into 8 wedges (about ¾-inch thick))
1 small red onion (about 8 ounces, cut into 16 wedges (about ½-inch thick))
https://www.skinnytaste.com/bacon-wrappe.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Spray a large sheet pan with oil. Adjust the center rack and the top rack 6 inches from the heating element.
Season pork with 1 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon mustard. Lay the bacon halves on a cutting board next to each other.
Carefully lay the tenderloin over the bacon. Tightly roll up the pork jelly-roll style. Tie the roast at 2- inch intervals with kitchen string each about 12-inches long to keep the bacon on the pork.
In a large bowl, toss together the delicata squash, Bartlett pear, red onion, olive oil, maple syrup, 1 tablespoon whole grain mustard and 1 teaspoons salt.
Place the pork tenderloin in the center of the sheet pan then arrange the vegetables and pears around the pork.
Roast in the oven until the center of the thickest piece of pork reaches 145°F with a meat thermometer and the vegetables and pears are tender, about 25 minutes.
Broil on the upper rack about 5 minutes, to brown the bacon and caramelize the vegetables (careful not to burn).
Remove from the oven and let it rest 5 minutes. Slice the pork against the grain into 12 slices then divide the vegetables and pear wedges among 4 plates.

4 cups butternut squash (peeled, seeded and cut into ¾-inch cubes (about 1 medium squash))
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper (to taste)
3 cups chicken broth (or chicken bone broth, plus more to thin if desired)
Optional toppings: sliced avocado (additional cilantro, lime wedges, sliced jalapeño, and coconut sour cream)

Prepare: Have the chicken cooked and shredded and all vegetables chopped before beginning.
Sauté the squash: Heat the avocado oil or ghee in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the squash and season lightly with salt and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the aromatics: Add the onion and both bell peppers. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until beginning to soften. Add the garlic, jalapeño, cumin, oregano, chili powder, and chipotle. Cook for 30–60 seconds, stirring, until fragrant.
Simmer: Add the green chiles and 3 cups broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Partially cover and cook for about 10–15 minutes, or until the squash is fork-tender. Larger or firmer cubes may need additional time.
Heat the chicken: Stir in the shredded chicken and optional nutritional yeast. Simmer for about 5 minutes, until the chicken is heated through; refrigerated cooked chicken should reach 165°F. Add more broth if desired. For thicker chili, mash a few cooked squash pieces into the broth.
Finish and serve: Remove from the heat and stir in the lime juice and cilantro. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Serve with your choice of toppings.

Pat the chicken dry and season with ½ teaspoon salt and the black pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in two batches, approximately 3–4 minutes per batch, adding more of the oil as needed. Transfer to a plate; the chicken will finish cooking in the soup.
Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining oil as needed. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, Italian seasoning, and optional red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the squash, broth, and remaining ½ teaspoon salt. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Partially cover and cook for 8–10 minutes, until the squash begins to soften.
Return the chicken and any accumulated juices to the pot. Simmer gently, partially covered, for another 7–10 minutes, or until the squash is tender and the largest chicken pieces reach 165°F. Larger squash pieces may require additional time.
Stir in the coconut milk and optional nutritional yeast, followed by the spinach. Warm gently for 2–3 minutes, until the spinach wilts. Avoid boiling.
Stir in 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Taste and add the second teaspoon if needed, along with additional salt and pepper to taste. Add a splash of broth if the soup is too thick. Garnish with optional basil and serve.

https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/meatb.description: This hearty Meatball Orzo Soup is made with tender homemade meatballs, orzo, vegetables, spinach, fire-roasted tomatoes, and Parmesan in a flavorful tomato broth. It’s an easy one-pot dinner the whole family will love!

ingredients: 1/2 lb. ground beef, (can use ground turkey)
1 red bell pepper, (seeds removed and diced)
Kosher salt and black pepper, (to taste)
1/2 lb. ground beef, (can use ground turkey)
1 red bell pepper, (seeds removed and diced)
Kosher salt and black pepper, (to taste)
https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/meatb.instructions:
Make the meatball mixture. In a large bowl, combine ground beef (or turkey), sausage, egg, breadcrumbs, parmesan cheese, garlic, fresh parsley, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Gently toss with hands until all ingredients are evenly distributed.
Form the meatballs. Roll the mixture into tablespoon-size meatballs and transfer to a large plate.
Brown the meatballs. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium high heat. Add half of the meatballs and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until browned on all sides, turning occasionally. They don’t have to be cooked all the way through because they will finish cooking in the soup. Transfer cooked meatballs to a plate lined with paper towels. Repeat the process with remaining meatballs.
Cook the veggies. In a large pot, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium high heat. Add onion, carrots, celery, and red pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, or until veggies have softened. Add garlic and cook for one more minute.
Assemble soup. Poor in the broth and fire roasted tomatoes bring to a boil. Season soup with Italian seasoning, bay leaf, salt, and pepper, to taste. Add in the orzo and meatballs, reduce the heat to low.
Simmer. Cover the pot with a lid and cook for about 10 minutes or until pasta is tender and meatballs are cooked through.
Add spinach and parmesan. Stir in spinach, parmesan cheese, and crushed red pepper flakes. Cook for one more minute. Remove the bay leaf.
Serve. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with freshly grated parmesan cheese, if desired. Enjoy!

https://www.wellplated.com/buffalo-chick.description: This Buffalo chicken pasta is creamy, cheesy, and perfectly spicy. An easy 25-minute dinner that cooks in one pot for minimal cleanup!

ingredients: 1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs (cut into ½-inch pieces)
4 ounces cream cheese or Neufchâtel (cut into chunks and softened to room temperature)
¼ cup Buffalo sauce (such as Frank's RedHot, plus additional for serving)
2 ounces shredded sharp cheddar (about ¼ cup*)
1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs (cut into ½-inch pieces)
4 ounces cream cheese or Neufchâtel (cut into chunks and softened to room temperature)
¼ cup Buffalo sauce (such as Frank's RedHot, plus additional for serving)
2 ounces shredded sharp cheddar (about ¼ cup*)
https://www.wellplated.com/buffalo-chick.instructions:
Season
In a medium bowl, toss the chicken with the garlic powder, onion powder, dill, cayenne, and salt until evenly coated.
Brown
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Once it's hot, add the butter and let melt. Add the chicken in a single layer and brown on all sides until golden, about 4 minutes. (It does not need to be cooked through.)
Add the tomatoes with their liquid, broth, and pasta. Stir, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Cover and bring to a simmer. (The pasta won't be fully submerged). Once simmering, uncover and stir, then replace the lid and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Simmer 10 to 12 minutes, uncovering to stir every 3 to 4 minutes then covering again, until the pasta is al dente.
Stir
Turn off the heat. Add the Buffalo sauce and cream cheese, stirring until smooth.
Add the mozzarella and cheddar a handful at a time, stirring until each addition melts before adding the next (do not add it too quickly, or the cheese may lump). Taste and adjust the seasoning as desired.
Serve hot, topped with green onions and an additional drizzle of Buffalo sauce to taste.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/pumpkin-curr.description: This easy Pumpkin Curry recipe is a creamy vegan dinner made with fresh pumpkin, canned pumpkin, coconut milk, and warm spices. Cozy and budget-friendly!

ingredients: 1 pie pumpkin (seeds removed, skin removed & small dice, (about 2 lbs., 4 cups) $2.62*)
13.66 oz. can full-fat unsweetened coconut milk ($2.99)
15 oz. can 100% pumpkin puree (not pumpkin pie filling, $1.96***)
1 pie pumpkin (seeds removed, skin removed & small dice, (about 2 lbs., 4 cups) $2.62*)

https://www.budgetbytes.com/pumpkin-curr.instructions:
Prep the pumpkin
Gather and prepare all ingredients. Using a chef’s knife, carefully cut the pie pumpkin in half from top to bottom, starting right beside the stem. Use a spoon to scoop out the seeds and stringy pulp. (Save the seeds for roasting, if you'd like!)
Dice the pumpkin
Cut away the stem and the small piece of the bottom. Place the pumpkin halves cut-side down, then cut each half into ½"-wide wedges. Then, using your knife, remove the skin from each wedge and dice into small cubes. Continue until all of the pumpkin is diced.
Saute the pumpkin
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, add the cubed pumpkin and onions in an even layer. Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the rice
While the pumpkin and onions are cooking, you can start the rice. Add the rice and water to a medium pot and cook it according to the package instructions. Set aside when finished.
Add the aromatics
After the pumpkin and onions have cooked for about 10 minutes, add the garlic and ginger and sauté for 1-2 minutes until aromatic.
Bloom the tomato paste
Next, add the tomato paste and continue cooking for another 1-2 minutes.
Add the seasonings
Sprinkle in the garam masala, curry powder, cumin, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.
Simmer the curry
Pour in the coconut milk and pumpkin puree. Stir to combine. Bring the curry to a simmer and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add brown sugar
Then, stir in the brown sugar until dissolved.
Add broth and taste
Lastly, pour in the vegetable broth and stir to combine. Taste and adjust for seasoning and texture. Feel free to add an additional splash of broth.
Serve with rice
Serve the pumpkin curry over the rice with desired toppings, then enjoy!

ingredients: ▢ 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil or melted vegan butter, plus more for drizzling
▢ 1¼ cups unsweetened almond milk, plus more if necessary
▢ ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
▢ ¼ cup fresh sage leaves, for garnish
▢ ½ cup pecans, plus more for garnish
▢ ½ cup walnuts, plus more for garnish
▢ 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil or melted vegan butter

https://www.loveandlemons.com/vegan-swee.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with foil and brush a 9x13-inch baking dish with olive oil.
Use a fork to poke a few holes into the sweet potatoes. Place on the baking sheet and roast until very tender, about 60 minutes.
Make the crumble topping: In a food processor, place the oats, pecans, walnuts, garlic, maple syrup, olive oil, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper and pulse until just combined. Remove and set aside.
Scoop the cooked sweet potato flesh out of the skins and place in a food processor. Add the olive oil, milk, ginger, salt, and pepper and process to combine. Spread the mixture into the baking dish.
Sprinkle with the crumble topping, additional nuts, and sage leaves. Drizzle with olive oil and bake for 20 minutes, or until the topping is browned and crisp.

https://www.wellplated.com/taco-rice/.description: Taco rice combines seasoned beef, rice, beans, salsa, and cheese in one pot. This easy, flavorful dinner is perfect for busy weeknights.

ingredients: 1 pound 93% lean ground beef (or ground turkey)
1 cup long grain white rice (such as Jasmine or Basmati, rinsed and drained)
⅔ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese (or Monterey Jack or pepper Jack, plus additional for serving)
Chopped cilantro, sliced green onion, plain Greek yogurt (or sour cream), crushed tortilla chips, and/or avocado for serving
1 pound 93% lean ground beef (or ground turkey)
1 cup long grain white rice (such as Jasmine or Basmati, rinsed and drained)

Chopped cilantro, sliced green onion, plain Greek yogurt (or sour cream), crushed tortilla chips, and/or avocado for serving

Brown
Heat a Dutch oven or similar large, deep skillet over medium-high. Once the skillet is hot, add the oil and let warm for a minute. Add the beef, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper. Let brown, breaking the meat into crumbles, until fully cooked through. Taste to adjust the seasoning.
Stir in the rice, beef broth, salsa, black beans, and green chiles.
Simmer
Increase the heat and bring the liquid to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and let cook gently for 15 minutes (If your lid has a steam hole, cover it with foil, or the rice will not cook properly. You want all of the steam trapped.)
Check the rice - most of the liquid should be absorbed and if you take a small bite from the center, the rice should be tender. If not, recover and continue cooking, adding a little water if needed.
Rest
Once the rice is tender, remove from the heat, cover, and let rest five minutes (this step is important to make sure your rice is nice and fluffy).
Add
Stir in the cheese. Divide into bowls and top with more cheese, cilantro, green onion, Greek yogurt, avocado, or any other desired toppings.

https://www.spendwithpennies.com/philly-.description: Philly Cheesesteak Casserole combines seasoned ground beef, peppers, mushrooms, and tender pasta in a rich homemade cheese sauce. Pepper jack melts over the top for a bubbly, cheesy finish.

ingredients: 2 teaspoons steak seasoning (such as Montreal steak spice)
8 ounces brown mushrooms (or white mushrooms, sliced)
1 large green bell pepper (seeded and sliced)
⅔ cup half and half (or evaporated milk)
2 teaspoons steak seasoning (such as Montreal steak spice)
8 ounces brown mushrooms (or white mushrooms, sliced)
1 large green bell pepper (seeded and sliced)
⅔ cup half and half (or evaporated milk)
https://www.spendwithpennies.com/philly-.instructions:
Preheat oven to 350℉. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Once water is boiling, add pasta and cook until al dente, according to package directions. Drain well and transfer to the prepared baking dish.
While the pasta is cooking, heat a large 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook for 2 to 3 minutes without stirring to form a crust. Continue cooking, breaking the meat up with a spoon, until no longer pink. Stir in the steak seasoning. Transfer the beef to the prepared baking dish, leaving a teaspoon of the grease in the skillet.
Add the onions, mushrooms, and peppers to the skillet and cook until tender, about 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer to the baking dish.
To the same skillet over medium heat, add the butter and flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the beef broth, stirring after each addition until smooth. Add the half-and-half, Dijon mustard, bouillon cube, and pepper. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes or until thickened. Remove from the heat and whisk in the Swiss cheese and ½ cup of pepper jack cheese until smooth.
Pour the sauce over the pasta, beef, and veggies in the baking dish and toss to coat. Spread the remaining 1 cup of pepper jack cheese over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until bubbly and cheese is melted.

Everything roasts together on one pan for an easy weeknight dinner with big flavor and minimal cleanup. Serve over rice and finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless, (skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces)
1 1/2 pounds boneless, (skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces)
https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/sheet.instructions:
Prep. Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or spray with nonstick cooking spray.
Make the Sauce. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, sriracha, and water.
Assemble. Place the chicken, broccoli, bell peppers, and onion on the prepared baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and season lightly with salt and black pepper. Pour the sauce over the chicken and vegetables and toss until everything is well coated. Spread everything into an even single layer, making sure the chicken and vegetables aren't too crowded.
Roast. Roast for 20 minutes, tossing halfway through, or until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
Serve. Serve warm over rice. Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.

ingredients: ½ cup chopped oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes (drained)
2 Tablespoons all-purpose flour (or gluten-free all-purpose flour)
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (plus more for serving)
½ cup chopped oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes (drained)
2 Tablespoons all-purpose flour (or gluten-free all-purpose flour)
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (plus more for serving)
https://www.eatingbirdfood.com/slow-cook.instructions:
Add chicken
Place the chicken breasts in the slow cooker in a single layer. Season with Italian seasoning, garlic powder ,salt, paprika and pepper.
Add broth
Sprinkle the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes over the chicken. Pour the chicken broth around the chicken.
Cook chicken
Cover and cook on low for 3–4 hours or on high for 1.5-2 hours, until the chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. Avoid overcooking, as chicken breasts can dry out.
Transfer the cooked chicken to a plate and set aside, leaving the broth and juices in the slow cooker.
Make roux
Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk continuously for about 1 minute, until smooth and lightly bubbling.
Whisk roux
Slowly whisk the heavy cream into the roux. Cook for 2–3 minutes, whisking frequently, until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened. Stir in the Parmesan and red pepper flakes and cook until the Parmesan is melted.
Add roux to slow cooker
Pour the cream sauce into the slow cooker and stir it into the broth and cooking juices. Stir in the spinach and let it sit for a few minutes with the slow cooker on low or warm, until wilted.
Serve
Return the chicken to the slow cooker and spoon the sauce over top. Serve warm over pasta, rice or mashed potatoes, or with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce. Garnish with fresh basil and additional Parmesan, if desired.

https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/chicke.description: Juicy chicken thighs, roasted Brussels sprouts, and crispy bacon in a creamy garlic Dijon sauce. Includes a dairy-free sauce and a heavy cream and Parmesan variation.

ingredients: 1½ pounds Brussels sprouts (trimmed and halved, or quartered if very large)
1½ tablespoons olive oil or avocado oil
¾ teaspoon fine sea salt (divided, plus more to taste)
1½ pounds boneless (skinless chicken thighs, cut into approximately 1-inch pieces)
1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (or ½ teaspoon dried thyme)
¾ cup canned full-fat coconut milk (thoroughly stirred)
1½ pounds Brussels sprouts (trimmed and halved, or quartered if very large)
1½ tablespoons olive oil or avocado oil
¾ teaspoon fine sea salt (divided, plus more to taste)
1½ pounds boneless (skinless chicken thighs, cut into approximately 1-inch pieces)
1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (or ½ teaspoon dried thyme)
¾ cup canned full-fat coconut milk (thoroughly stirred)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/chicke.instructions:
Roast the sprouts. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Toss the Brussels sprouts with the oil, ¼ teaspoon salt, and ¼ teaspoon pepper on a large rimmed sheet pan. Arrange in a single layer with cut sides down. Roast for 22–28 minutes, until browned and tender, checking smaller sprouts early.
Cook the bacon. Meanwhile, cook the chopped bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Leave approximately 2 tablespoons bacon fat in the skillet and spoon out any excess.
Cook the chicken. Pat the chicken dry and season with the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper. Heat the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in two batches, approximately 5–7 minutes per batch, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through to 165°F. Transfer to a plate. Add a little oil if needed.
Cook the onion. Reduce the heat to medium and leave approximately 1 tablespoon fat in the skillet. Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 30 seconds.
Make the sauce. Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Stir in the coconut milk, Dijon, and optional nutritional yeast. Bring to a gentle simmer. Mix the tapioca starch with the cold water, then stir into the sauce. Simmer gently for about 1 minute, just until lightly thickened. Avoid prolonged boiling.
Combine and serve. Return the chicken and accumulated juices to the skillet. Gently fold in the roasted sprouts and half the bacon. Heat for 1–2 minutes, just until hot. Add 1 teaspoon lemon juice, then taste and adjust the lemon, salt, and pepper. If needed, add a little broth to loosen the sauce. Sprinkle with the remaining bacon and serve.

https://minimalistbaker.com/cheesy-vegan.description: Enchiladas, in a hurry! This easy, 30-minute vegan enchilada skillet is hearty and flavorful with sweet potato or winter squash, black beans, rich red enchilada sauce, and a “cheesy” vegan cashew sauce!

ingredients: 1/2 small clove garlic (or 1/8 tsp garlic powder)
2 Tbsp tapioca starch (also called tapioca flour)
ingredient_groups.purpose: CASHEW “CHEESE” (or sub shredded vegan or dairy cheese*)

ingredients: 1/2 medium yellow or white onion, diced (1/2 medium onion yields ~1 heaping cup or 150 g)
4 medium cloves garlic, minced (4 medium cloves yield ~2 Tbsp or 18 g)
2 cups sweet potato or kabocha squash, peeled, diced into 1/4-1/2-inch cubes*
1 medium poblano pepper, stemmed, seeded, and diced into 1/2-inch squares (or green bell pepper // 1 pepper yields ~1/2 cup or 75 g)
1 (15-oz.) can black beans, drained and rinsed
4 (4-inch) corn tortillas*, sliced into 1/4-inch x 2-inch strips
1/2 small clove garlic (or 1/8 tsp garlic powder)
2 Tbsp tapioca starch (also called tapioca flour)
1/2 medium yellow or white onion, diced (1/2 medium onion yields ~1 heaping cup or 150 g)
4 medium cloves garlic, minced (4 medium cloves yield ~2 Tbsp or 18 g)
2 cups sweet potato or kabocha squash, peeled, diced into 1/4-1/2-inch cubes*
1 medium poblano pepper, stemmed, seeded, and diced into 1/2-inch squares (or green bell pepper // 1 pepper yields ~1/2 cup or 75 g)
1 (15-oz.) can black beans, drained and rinsed
4 (4-inch) corn tortillas*, sliced into 1/4-inch x 2-inch strips
https://minimalistbaker.com/cheesy-vegan.instructions:
Start by cooking the veggies for the skillet. Heat a large (preferably oven-safe) skillet over medium heat. Once hot, add oil and onion and sauté for a few minutes until translucent. Add the sea salt and garlic and cook for another 1-2 minutes.
Next, add the sweet potato (or squash) and pepper. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until they are starting to soften — about 5 minutes.
Add the drained and rinsed black beans (or pinto beans) and tortilla strips and stir.
Finally, add the enchilada sauce, stir well, and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, cover and lower the heat to medium-low. Cook for ~10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potato (or squash) is tender when pierced with a fork.
Meanwhile, to a small high-speed blender, add the cashew sauce ingredients (cashews, water, lime juice, garlic, tapioca starch, and sea salt). Blend on high until smooth and creamy.
After the skillet has sautéed and your squash/sweet potatoes are tender, remove the lid, reduce the heat to low, and carefully pour the cashew sauce (or sprinkle shredded cheese) over the beans in an even layer. Cover and steam for 3-5 minutes to encourage the cheese to firm up (or melt) a bit. Then remove the lid and (optionally) transfer to the oven to broil for another 2-3 minutes, or until the cheese is darkened in spots and dry to the touch.
Serve warm garnished with green onions and cilantro (both optional). Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days or in the freezer for 1 month (or longer).
Freezing: You can freeze the enchilada skillet in individual containers for quicker reheating or freeze the entire dish. To freeze in individual containers, transfer individual servings to freezer-safe containers (we like glass storage containers), let cool in the refrigerator, then cover with a lid or foil and freeze. When ready to eat, uncover and microwave using the defrost then full power settings to heat until warmed through. To freeze the entire dish, transfer to a large freezer-safe container (such as a casserole dish), let cool in the refrigerator, then cover and transfer to the freezer. When ready to eat/serve, defrost overnight in the refrigerator, then bake in a 350 degree F (176 C) oven until warmed through.

ingredients: 2 medium boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 6 to 8 ounces each)
¼ teaspoon fine sea salt (increase to ½ teaspoon if you are not brining)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 medium boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 6 to 8 ounces each)
¼ teaspoon fine sea salt (increase to ½ teaspoon if you are not brining)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/air-fryer-.instructions:
Brine the chicken, if desired. Stir together the lukewarm water and salt in a medium bowl until the salt is dissolved. Add the chicken breasts and let them brine for 15 minutes at room temperature. Alternatively, cover and refrigerate for up to 30 minutes. Remove the chicken from the brine, rinse it briefly under cool water, then thoroughly pat it dry with paper towels.
Even out the chicken breasts. Place the chicken breasts between two sheets of parchment paper or plastic wrap. Use a meat mallet or rolling pin to gently pound the thicker portions until each breast is an even ¾-inch thickness.
Preheat the air fryer. Heat the air fryer to 375°F for 3 to 5 minutes, or according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Season the chicken. Brush the chicken breasts evenly on both sides with the olive oil. In a small bowl, stir together the salt, garlic powder, smoked paprika and black pepper. Sprinkle the seasoning mixture evenly over both sides of the chicken and gently rub it into the surface.
Air-fry the chicken. Arrange the chicken breasts in a single layer in the air fryer basket, leaving space between them for the air to circulate. Air-fry at 375°F for 10 to 14 minutes, flipping halfway through cooking, until the thickest part of each breast reaches 160°F on an instant-read thermometer. Cooking time will depend on the size of your chicken breast and your brand of air fryer, so keep a close eye on the temperature to avoid overcooking.
Rest. Transfer the chicken to a clean plate and loosely tent it with foil. Let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes, during which the internal temperature should rise to 165°F.
Serve. Slice the chicken against the grain and serve warm.

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/chicken-to.description: This chicken tortilla soup features a tomato broth blended with pasilla and guajillo chiles, shredded chicken, black beans and crispy tortilla strips.

ingredients: 1 large dried pasilla chile (stemmed and seeded)
2 tablespoons avocado oil or olive oil (divided)
4 cups chicken stock (divided, plus more as needed)
2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lime juice (plus more to taste)
fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Toppings: diced or sliced avocado, crumbled queso fresco or shredded Mexican-blend cheese, Mexican crema or sour cream, chopped fresh cilantro, lime wedges
1 large dried pasilla chile (stemmed and seeded)
2 tablespoons avocado oil or olive oil (divided)
4 cups chicken stock (divided, plus more as needed)
2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lime juice (plus more to taste)
fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Toppings: diced or sliced avocado, crumbled queso fresco or shredded Mexican-blend cheese, Mexican crema or sour cream, chopped fresh cilantro, lime wedges
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/chicken-to.instructions:
Toast the chiles. Heat a large Dutch oven or stockpot over medium heat. Add the pasilla and guajillo chiles and toast for 10 to 15 seconds per side, pressing them gently against the pan, until fragrant and slightly softened. Take care not to let them blacken or burn.
Soak the chiles. Transfer the toasted chiles to a heatproof bowl, cover with very hot water and let soak for 5-10 minutes. Drain well.
Sauté the aromatics. While the chiles are soaking, add 1 tablespoon oil to the pot and heat over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened. Add the garlic and sauté for 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Blend the tomato-chile purée. Transfer the onion and garlic to a blender. Add the softened chiles, fire-roasted tomatoes with their juices and 1 cup of the chicken stock. Blend for 1 to 2 minutes, until completely smooth.
Fry the purée. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil to the pot and heat over medium-high heat. Carefully pour in the tomato-chile purée; it may splatter, so pour slowly. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. (You can cover the pot partially with a lid during this process to prevent splattering.)
Simmer the soup. Stir in the remaining 3 cups chicken stock and the oregano. Bring the soup to a gentle simmer. Add the shredded chicken and black beans, reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a splash of additional chicken stock if you prefer a thinner, brothier soup.
Season the soup. Remove the soup from the heat and stir in 2 tablespoons lime juice. Taste and season with salt, black pepper and additional lime juice as needed. The soup should taste bright and well seasoned before serving.
Fry the tortilla strips. While the soup simmers, stack the corn tortillas and slice them into thin strips. Pour about ¼ inch of neutral oil into a skillet and heat over medium-high heat until shimmering. Working in batches, fry the tortilla strips for 1 to 2 minutes, turning as needed, until crisp and golden. Transfer them using a slotted spoon to a paper-towel-lined plate and immediately sprinkle with fine sea salt.
Serve. Divide a handful of tortilla strips among the serving bowls and ladle the hot soup over them. Top with avocado, queso fresco, crema, cilantro and additional tortilla strips. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/turke.description: Turkey pumpkin pasta bake is a comforting fall casserole made with ground turkey, pasta, a creamy pumpkin herb sauce, ricotta, and plenty of melted mozzarella and Parmesan. It's savory, cheesy, and perfect for an easy weeknight dinner or cozy Sunday meal.

ingredients: 1 pound pasta, (such as rigatoni, penne, or ziti)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 pound pasta, (such as rigatoni, penne, or ziti)

https://www.twopeasandtheirpod.com/turke.instructions:
Preheat the oven. Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish and set aside.
Cook the pasta. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until just shy of al dente according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Cook the turkey. In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 4 minutes. Add the ground turkey and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned and cooked through, about 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in the garlic, sage, rosemary, thyme, and crushed red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute. Season with salt and black pepper.
Make the pumpkin sauce. Add the pumpkin puree, chicken broth, and heavy cream to the skillet. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Stir in the Parmesan and nutmeg. Season to taste with salt and black pepper. Stir in the cooked pasta.
Make the ricotta mixture. In a medium bowl, stir together the ricotta, egg, Parmesan, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Assemble in Pan. Add half of the pasta mixture to the prepared baking dish and dollop half of the ricotta mixture over the top. Sprinkle with half of the mozzarella cheese. Add the remaining pasta mixture, followed by the remaining ricotta mixture and mozzarella. Sprinkle with the Parmesan.
Bake. Cover the baking dish loosely with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for another 10 to 15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly. For a more golden top, broil for 1 to 2 minutes, watching carefully.
Serve. Let the pasta bake rest for 5 to 10 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley and, if desired, a little additional Parmesan.

ingredients: 3 cups chopped carrots (about 6 large carrots or 16 oz bag baby carrots)
½ teaspoon black pepper (plus more to taste)
1 teaspoon dried thyme (or 1 Tablespoon fresh thyme)
½ teaspoon dried rosemary (or 1 ½ teaspoons fresh rosemary)

1 medium cauliflower head (chopped into large chunks)
¼ cup all-purpose flour (or gluten-free all-purpose flour)

Add the chicken breasts, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, salt, pepper, thyme, rosemary and broth to a 6-quart or larger slow cooker. Stir the vegetables and broth around the chicken, making sure the chicken is mostly submerged. Nestle the large cauliflower florets on top.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6–7 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours, until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F and the vegetables and cauliflower are tender.
Remove the chicken and transfer to a cutting board. Chop into bite-size pieces and set aside.

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/falafel-re.description: Homemade falafel made with soaked dried chickpeas, fresh parsley and cilantro, garlic, lemon and warm spices, fried until deeply golden and crisp. Serve warm with tahini sauce, pita and fresh vegetables.

ingredients: 1 cup dried chickpeas (do not use canned)
1 small lemon (zested and juiced (about 2 tablespoons juice))
1 cup packed fresh cilantro (mostly leaves plus some tender stems)
1 cup packed fresh parsley (mostly leaves plus some tender stems)
¼ cup all-purpose flour (plus 1–2 extra tablespoons if mixture feels wet)
neutral oil for frying (e.g., avocado, canola, grapeseed)
1 cup dried chickpeas (do not use canned)
1 small lemon (zested and juiced (about 2 tablespoons juice))
1 cup packed fresh cilantro (mostly leaves plus some tender stems)
1 cup packed fresh parsley (mostly leaves plus some tender stems)
¼ cup all-purpose flour (plus 1–2 extra tablespoons if mixture feels wet)
neutral oil for frying (e.g., avocado, canola, grapeseed)
https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/falafel-re.instructions:
Soak the chickpeas. Place dried chickpeas in a large bowl, cover with plenty of cold water, and soak 18-24 hours (they’ll triple in size). Drain well and pat dry.
Make the falafel mixture. In a food processor, pulse chickpeas, onion, garlic, lemon zest and juice, cilantro, parsley, cumin, coriander, cayenne, salt, and pepper until finely minced but not puréed. Add flour and baking powder; pulse briefly to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Chill 30–60 minutes for best shaping.
Shape. Using damp hands or a small scoop, form ~2 Tbsp portions into balls or patties. If mixture is sticky, work in up to 1–2 more Tbsp flour.
Fry. Heat 2 inches of oil in a deep skillet to 350°F. Fry falafel 3–4 minutes per side until deeply golden and crisp. Strain using a spider strainer and transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Serve. Enjoy warm with tahini sauce, pickled onions, fresh veggies, or tucked in pita

https://www.spendwithpennies.com/brothy-.description: This viral brothy rice is a cozy bowl of sweet-tangy lime chicken and fluffy rice in a savory ginger-garlic broth

ingredients: 1.5 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs (or chicken breast cutlets)
2 green onions (sliced, greens and whites divided)
chili crisp (or hoisin sauce for drizzling, sesame seeds, and/or cilantro)
1.5 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs (or chicken breast cutlets)
2 green onions (sliced, greens and whites divided)
chili crisp (or hoisin sauce for drizzling, sesame seeds, and/or cilantro)
https://www.spendwithpennies.com/brothy-.instructions:
For the chicken, in a large bowl, combine 2 tablespoons vegetable oil, lime juice, brown sugar, garlic, and salt. Add the chicken, mix well, and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes or up to 4 hours.
Thinly slice the green onions, dividing the whites and greens.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a deep non-stick skillet over medium heat. Remove the chicken from the marinade and let the excess drip off. Add it to the skillet and cook for 7 to 9 minutes, flipping the chicken occasionally, until browned and the center reaches 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and cover to keep warm.
In the meantime, in a large saucepan, add the broth, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and the whites of the green onions. Bring it to a boil over medium-high heat.
Whisk the 1 tablespoon of cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of water and add to the broth, reduce to a gentle boil, and cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
While simmering, slice the chicken into strips.
Divide the rice over the bowls, divide the broth over the bowls and top with chicken. Drizzle any juices over the chicken.
Garnish with the greens of the green onion, toasted sesame seeds, cilantro, hoisin sauce or chili crisp.

https://www.loveandlemons.com/pastina-so.description: This pastina soup recipe is filled with tiny pasta and tender vegetables. With its golden, flavorful broth, it's soothing, nourishing, and comforting. I love it when I'm under the weather or on any chilly day!

ingredients: ▢ 4 medium carrots, chopped into small pieces (2½ cups)
▢ 3 celery ribs, chopped into small pieces (1 cup)
▢ ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
▢ 6 fresh thyme sprigs, bundled, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
▢ 1 bunch fresh parsley, stems bundled, leaves chopped and reserved for garnish
▢ 1 Parmesan rind, plus freshly grated Parmesan for serving
▢ 4 medium carrots, chopped into small pieces (2½ cups)
▢ 3 celery ribs, chopped into small pieces (1 cup)
▢ ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
▢ 6 fresh thyme sprigs, bundled, or 1 teaspoon dried thyme
▢ 1 bunch fresh parsley, stems bundled, leaves chopped and reserved for garnish
▢ 1 Parmesan rind, plus freshly grated Parmesan for serving
https://www.loveandlemons.com/pastina-so.instructions:
Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery, ½ teaspoon of the salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes, or until softened.
Stir in the garlic, then add the thyme and parsley bundles, bay leaves, Parmesan rind, broth, and the remaining ¾ teaspoon salt. Stir, then bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to maintain a simmer and cook, uncovered, for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender. Remove and discard the Parmesan rind, bay leaves, and thyme and parsley bundles.
Use a slotted spoon to scoop 2 cups of the vegetables out of the pot. Transfer to a blender and add 1 cup of the broth. Allow to cool slightly, then blend until completely smooth. Stir the puree back into the pot.
Bring the soup to a vigorous simmer. Add the pastina and cook until tender, about 9 to 15 minutes depending on the type of pasta you’re using. Stir in the lemon juice and season to taste.
Serve topped with freshly grated Parmesan and chopped fresh parsley leaves.

Shape

Brown

Preheat your oven to 400°F. Lightly grease a 2½- to 3-quart baking dish, or use a large oven-safe skillet.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the green beans and cook for 5 minutes, or until just tender with a little bite. Thicker beans may need longer. Drain thoroughly and spread on a clean kitchen towel to release steam and excess moisture.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Leave 2 tablespoons bacon fat in the skillet, removing excess or adding a little avocado oil if needed.
Add the mushrooms and chopped onion. Cook over medium to medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned and the mushroom liquid has evaporated. Stir in the garlic, thyme, and sage; cook for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Separately, whisk the coconut milk and tapioca starch until smooth. For the dairy option, whisk 1 cup cold heavy cream with 1 tablespoon arrowroot starch instead. Stir your chosen mixture into the skillet. Season with salt and pepper and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, for 1–2 minutes, just until thickened enough to coat a spoon. Avoid prolonged boiling. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Fold in the drained green beans and half the bacon. Transfer to the baking dish, or spread evenly in the oven-safe skillet. Bake uncovered for approximately 15 minutes, until hot and bubbling around the edges.
While the casserole bakes, toss the sliced onion with the almond milk. In a separate bowl, combine the almond flour, tapioca starch, onion powder, and salt. Lift onions from the milk, letting excess drip off, then toss in the flour mixture. Shake off loose flour.
Heat the avocado oil in a separate skillet over medium heat until shimmering, not smoking. Fry the onions in 2–3 batches in a loose single layer, approximately 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Adjust the heat if they brown too quickly, and add oil between batches as needed. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate.
Scatter the fried onions and remaining bacon over the hot casserole. Return to the oven for 3–5 minutes, watching closely to prevent burning. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds (680g) flank steak or skirt steak
1 pound fresh tomatillos (husks removed and rinsed)
1 jalapeño or serrano pepper (stem removed (seeded for less heat, if desired))
2 cups finely shredded green or red cabbage
1 1/2 pounds (680g) flank steak or skirt steak
1 pound fresh tomatillos (husks removed and rinsed)
1 jalapeño or serrano pepper (stem removed (seeded for less heat, if desired))

https://www.gimmesomeoven.com/steak-taco.instructions:
Marinate the steak. In a bowl or zip-top bag, whisk together the olive oil, lime juice, garlic, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Add the steak and toss to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
Make the salsa. Add the tomatillos, garlic, jalapeño, lime juice, avocado, cilantro, onion, water, salt, and cumin to a blender. Blend until smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Set aside.
Toss the cabbage. In a small bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Toss well and let sit for at least 10 minutes to soften slightly.
Cook the steak. Heat a grill or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the steak for 3–5 minutes per side, until nicely charred and cooked to your desired doneness (about 130–135°F for medium-rare). Transfer to a cutting board, rest for 5–10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Warm the tortillas. Warm the tortillas on a skillet or directly over a flame until soft and lightly charred.
Assemble the tacos. Fill each tortilla with sliced steak and a handful of limey cabbage. Top with chopped white onion and cilantro, then drizzle generously with the creamy salsa. Finish with a squeeze of lime and enjoy!

ingredients: ¾ cup turkey stock (chicken stock or broth, homemade or store-bought)
1 ½ cups seasoned dried stuffing mix (3 ½ ounces, such as Mrs Cubbisons)
½ small yellow onion (about 4 ounces, finely diced (about ¾ cup))
2 medium celery stalks (about 3 ½ ounces, finely diced (about ¾ cup))
1 teaspoon kosher salt (divided, plus additional to taste)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (divided)
1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh sage leaves
1 ¼ teaspoons poultry seasoning (I use Bells)
¼ cup grated parmesan cheese (about 3/4 ounce)
4 cups turkey stock (chicken stock or broth, homemade or store-bought, plus additional if needed)
1 teaspoon kosher salt (plus additional to taste)
½ teaspoon poultry seasoning (I use Bells)
¾ cup turkey stock (chicken stock or broth, homemade or store-bought)
1 ½ cups seasoned dried stuffing mix (3 ½ ounces, such as Mrs Cubbisons)
½ small yellow onion (about 4 ounces, finely diced (about ¾ cup))
2 medium celery stalks (about 3 ½ ounces, finely diced (about ¾ cup))
1 teaspoon kosher salt (divided, plus additional to taste)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (divided)
1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh sage leaves
1 ¼ teaspoons poultry seasoning (I use Bells)
¼ cup grated parmesan cheese (about 3/4 ounce)

https://www.skinnytaste.com/thanksgiving.instructions:
Make the meatballs: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the egg and stock until smooth and well-combined. Add the stuffing mix, stir to combine, and set aside to let the stuffing soften.
In a medium skillet, warm the olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion, celery,½ teaspoon salt, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Add the garlic, sage, poultry seasoning, and 2 teaspoons of water and cook, stirring constantly, until tender, about 2 minutes. Scrape the mixture into the bowl of softened stuffing mix and chill in the refrigerator until the sautéed vegetables are completely cooled, about 10 minutes.
When cool add the ground turkey, grated parmesan cheese, and remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper. Use wet hands to mix until well-combined.
Since the seasoning of the meatball mix will depend heavily on the brand of stuffing you use, cook off a small tester patty of the mix and taste for seasoning. Adjust the meatball mixture with more salt if needed. Using wet hands, form 30 small meatballs the size of a ping pong ball (about 2 tablespoons each), placing the meatballs onto a large sheet pan covered with foil (sprayed with oil) as you form them.
Arrange a rack in the upper third of the oven and turn on the broiler. Broil the meatballs until the top and sides are browned, about 5 to 6 minutes, careful not to burn. Set aside.
Make the gravy: Meanwhile, in a large pot over medium heat, combine 3 ½ cups of the turkey or chicken stock with the sage, thyme, salt (use less if your stock is salted) and black pepper to taste and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 15 minutes. Discard the herbs.
Meanwhile, in a blender add the remaining ½ cup of cold or room temperature stock with the flour and poultry seasoning and blend until smooth. Add 1 cup of the hot stock into the blender to temper and blend again, then pour into the pot with the simmering stock, whisking until thickened, 2 minutes. Add the butter and whisk until melted, taste for salt and adjust as needed.
Gently transfer the browned meatballs into the simmering gravy and cook, covered, for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, uncovering the last 5 minutes, to thicken.
Transfer the meatballs and gravy into a large serving bowl or platter, garnish with parsley, and serve hot.

ingredients: 1½ pounds boneless (skinless chicken thighs, excess fat trimmed)
1 teaspoon fine sea salt (divided, plus more to taste)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more to taste)
3 pounds yellow onions (weighed before peeling, peeled, halved, and sliced approximately ⅛ inch thick)

½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (plus more to taste)

½ cup dry white wine (or additional broth)

1 teaspoon balsamic vinegar (plus more to taste)
6 slices sturdy gluten-free bread (sized or trimmed to fit the bowls*)

Fresh thyme leaves and black pepper (for serving)
https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/french.instructions:
Brown the chicken: Pat the chicken dry and season with ½ teaspoon salt and the black pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large, heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for approximately 3 minutes per side, working in batches if necessary. Transfer to a plate; it will finish cooking in the soup.
Soften the onions: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, sliced onions, and remaining ½ teaspoon salt. Cook for 10–15 minutes, stirring frequently, until softened and beginning to collapse. If the browned bits on the bottom threaten to burn, add a small splash of water and scrape them up.
Caramelize: Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue cooking for approximately 30–45 minutes longer, until the onions are deeply golden and very soft. Stir every few minutes, more frequently toward the end. Add water 1–2 tablespoons at a time if the bottom gets too dark. Allow extra time if needed; use the color and texture as your guide.
Deglaze: Stir in the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the wine or additional broth and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Simmer: Add 5 cups broth, the bay leaf, and the chicken with its accumulated juices. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat and simmer partially covered for 18–25 minutes, until the chicken is tender and reaches at least 165°F in the thickest part.
Finish the soup: Transfer the chicken to a clean plate and shred into bite-size pieces. Return it to the pot and discard the bay leaf. Stir in the balsamic vinegar. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Add up to 1 additional cup broth if desired and a little more vinegar only if needed.
Toast the bread: While the soup simmers, preheat the oven to 425°F. Lightly brush both sides of the bread with olive oil and place on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake for 8–12 minutes, flipping halfway through, until crisp on both sides. Check early, as gluten-free breads vary.
Melt the cheese: Switch the oven to broil. Divide the grated Gruyère evenly among the toasts. Broil on the baking sheet for approximately 1–3 minutes, watching continuously, until the cheese is melted and lightly golden.
Serve: Ladle the hot soup into bowls and add a cheese toast to each serving. Finish with fresh thyme and black pepper and serve immediately.

Press the tofu: Wrap each block in a clean kitchen towel or several layers of paper towels and set them on a plate. Place a second plate on top and weigh it down with something heavy like a cast iron skillet or several cans. Let sit 30 minutes.
Toss
Cut the pressed tofu into ¾-inch cubes. Place in a large bowl, and gently toss with the cornstarch and salt.
Brown
Heat a wide, deep skillet over medium-high. Once hot, add 2 tablespoons of the oil. Once the oil shimmers, add half of the tofu, arranging so the pieces do not touch. Let it cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes, until the bottom is a medium golden brown. Turn (I use a fish spatula to flip in sections) and continue cooking until crisp on most sides, 6-8 minutes total. Move to a plate. Repeat, adding 1 tablespoon oil and remaining tofu.
Heat
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the final tablespoon of oil, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste, and garlic. Stir constantly for 30 seconds, breaking up the paste and scraping any browned bits off the bottom.
Add
Stir in the Italian seasoning and Cajun seasoning.
Simmer
Stir in the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. Let simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens but is still saucy.
Stir in the spinach a small handful at a time, letting each addition wilt before adding the next.
Finish
Return the tofu to the skillet and fold it into the sauce just until coated and warmed through, about 1 minute. Taste and add salt as needed. Serve right away, sprinkled with basil, over rice or with naan.

instructions_list: Heat a large deep skillet over medium high heat. Add the ground beef and let it cook for 3 to 4 minutes without stirring to form a nice crust on one side. Break it up with a spoon, continue cooking until no pink remains. Drain any fat.

Add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes. Add the broth, scraping up any browned bits on the bottom of the pan. Add the cabbage, bell peppers, diced tomatoes with chiles, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, paprika, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
Stir, cover, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until the cabbage is tender.
Season with additional salt and pepper to taste and rest for 5 minutes.
Serve over rice or pasta if desired.

https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-and-.description: This creamy Chicken and Broccoli Skillet Lasagna recipe makes 6 servings in just 50 minutes! Tender chicken, broccoli, and cheesy noodles, all made in one pan.

ingredients: 1 lb. chicken breast (1-2 breasts, (sliced in half horizontally) $2.57*)
8 oz. lasagna noodles (broken into 2-inch pieces, (9-10 noodles) $0.92***)
1 lb. chicken breast (1-2 breasts, (sliced in half horizontally) $2.57*)

https://www.budgetbytes.com/chicken-and-.instructions:
Gather and prep
Gather all ingredients.
Season the chicken
Stir together salt, black pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and Italian seasoning in a small bowl. Slice chicken breast in half and season thoroughly with half of seasoning blend.
Prep the vegetables
Finely chop the broccoli, including the stems, dice the onion, and mince the garlic.
Cook the chicken
Heat olive oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until fully cooked through (165℉ internally). Remove and set aside.
Sauté the aromatics
Reduce heat to medium and In the same skillet, add onion and garlic and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Cook and simmer
Add chicken broth and broken noodles. Stir and press noodles down so they’re mostly submerged. Cover and simmer on medium-low for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the broccoli
Stir in the broccoli and reserved seasoning mixture. Cover and continue cooking for 4-5 minutes, or until the noodles are tender and the broccoli is bright green. The mixture should still look slightly loose. If needed, add a splash of water to loosen it.
Shred the chicken
While the noodles finish cooking, shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Make it creamy
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the heavy cream, Parmesan cheese, and shredded chicken until well combined and creamy. Be careful not to allow the mixture to boil to avoid curdling.
Broil the cheese
Sprinkle the mozzarella evenly over the top. Transfer the skillet to the oven and broil for 2-4 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly browned.
Rest and serve
Remove from the oven and allow to cool for 3-5 minutes before serving. Enjoy!

https://www.halfbakedharvest.com/spinach.description: Baked Garlic Butter Spinach Chicken Parmesan Meatballs with creamy garlic parmesan sauce, marinara, and melty mozzarella. An easy, cozy family dinner!

ingredients: 2 pounds ground chicken or ground pork
2 pounds ground chicken or ground pork
https://www.halfbakedharvest.com/spinach.instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a bowl, combine the chicken, panko, 1/3 cup parmesan, egg, and 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning. Season with salt and pepper, then mix until just combined. Coat your hands with olive oil and roll the mixture into meatballs, making 15–16 meatballs.
Arrange the meatballs in a baking dish. Bake for 15 minutes, until beginning to crisp on the outside.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, mix the heavy cream, 2/3 cup parmesan, and 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove the baking dish from the oven. Add the butter, garlic, and chili flakes to the hot dish. Let the garlic sizzle in the butter for 2 minutes. Add the spinach, then pour the marinara and parmesan cream sauce over everything. Gently stir the sauces around the meatballs and top with torn mozzarella.
Return the dish to the oven and bake for another 15 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through (165°F), the sauce is bubbling, and the cheese is melted.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over your favorite spaghetti. Top with fresh basil and enjoy!

https://www.skinnytaste.com/turkey-burge.description: These delicious Turkey Burgers are topped with caramelized apples, shallots, and melted Gruyère cheese for an easy, fall dinner.

ingredients: ¼ cup plain panko (or gluten-free panko)
1 medium sweet apple (such as Gala, cored and sliced thin, about 1 ½ cups)
2 large shallots (sliced into rings, about 1 cup)
¼ cup plain panko (or gluten-free panko)
1 medium sweet apple (such as Gala, cored and sliced thin, about 1 ½ cups)
2 large shallots (sliced into rings, about 1 cup)
https://www.skinnytaste.com/turkey-burge.instructions:
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the oil, shallots, apple, thyme and salt. Stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally until the apples and onions are tender, about 16 to 20 minutes. If the mixture starts to get too brown, add a splash of water, about 1 tablespoon at a time (I used 2 total). Transfer to a bowl and stir in the honey. Set aside.
Meanwhile make the burger patties, add all of the ingredients to a mixing bowl. Mix well to combine evenly. With wet hands, form the mixture into 4 equal patties.
Heat the large skillet over medium-high heat. Spray with oil and place the patties in the pan in an evenly layer. Cook for 3 minutes, then flip. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cover. Continue cooking until the burgers are cooked through, about 5 minutes then top with the gruyere cheese, cover until the cheese is melted, 1 minute more.
Remove from the pan and serve immediately topped with the apple and shallot mixture.
